title: Conditional DETR's `post_process_semantic_segmentation` removes one class
body:
### System Info

transformers 4.57.3
python 3.13.9

### Who can help?

@yonigozlan @molbap

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Let's run two identical models - DETR and Conditional DETR - with 100 classes

```py
import io
import requests
from PIL import Image
import torch
import numpy

from transformers import (
    AutoImageProcessor,
    ConditionalDetrConfig,
    ConditionalDetrForSegmentation,
)
from transformers.image_transforms import rgb_to_id

url = "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"
image = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw)

image_processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("microsoft/conditional-detr-resnet-50")

# randomly initialize all weights of the model
config = ConditionalDetrConfig(num_labels=100)
model = ConditionalDetrForSegmentation(config)

# prepare image for the model
inputs = image_processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")

# forward pass
cond_detr_outputs = model(**inputs)

# Use the `post_process_semantic_segmentation` method of the `image_processor` to retrieve post-processed semantic segmentation maps
cond_detr_result = image_processor.post_process_semantic_segmentation(cond_detr_outputs, target_sizes=[(300, 500)])
```

```py
import io
import requests
from PIL import Image
import torch
import numpy

from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, DetrForSegmentation, DetrConfig
from transformers.image_transforms import rgb_to_id

url = "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"
image = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw)

image_processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/detr-resnet-50-panoptic")

config = DetrConfig(num_labels=100)
model = DetrForSegmentation(config)

# prepare image for the model
inputs = image_processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")

# forward pass
detr_outputs = model(**inputs)

# Use the `post_process_semantic_segmentation` method of the `image_processor` to retrieve post-processed semantic segmentation maps
detr_result = image_processor.post_process_semantic_segmentation(detr_outputs, target_sizes=[(300, 500)])
```

Now let's look at the models outputs:

```py
>>> cond_detr_outputs.logits.shape
torch.Size([1, 300, 100])
```

```py
>>> detr_outputs.logits.shape
torch.Size([1, 100, 101])
```

As we can see, Conditional DETR logits contain 100 classes, and DETR logits contain 101 class (100 + null class)

However, both Conditional DETR and DETR `post_process_semantic_segmentation` functions are the same: they both treat the input data like there are n+1 classes in it:

```py
class_queries_logits = outputs.logits  # [batch_size, num_queries, num_classes+1]
...
# Remove the null class `[..., :-1]`
masks_classes = class_queries_logits.softmax(dim=-1)[..., :-1]
```

The function removes the last class, which is correct for DETR (which have an additional null class) and incorrect for Conditional DETR (which does not have a null class) and may result in losing information about the last actual class.


### Expected behavior

Do not remove the last class in Conditional DETR's `post_process_semantic_segmentation` function:

```py
masks_classes = class_queries_logits.softmax(dim=-1)
```

Feature Request

### Description

Add a fast image processor for VideoMAE (`VideoMAEImageProcessorFast`) that uses `torch` and `torchvision` instead of PIL/numpy for better inference performance.

### Motivation

- VideoMAE currently only has a slow image processor (`VideoMAEImageProcessor`) using PIL/numpy
- Adding a fast processor using torch/torchvision will significantly improve inference speed
- This aligns with the ongoing effort to add fast processors to vision models (referenced in #36978)
- Other similar models (ViT, DETR, etc.) already have fast processors

### Proposed Implementation

1. Create `src/transformers/models/videomae/image_processing_videomae_fast.py`
   - Inherit from `BaseImageProcessorFast`
   - Match the functionality of the existing slow processor
   
2. Update `src/transformers/models/videomae/__init__.py` to export the new class

3. Add tests to verify equivalence between slow and fast processors

### Example (based on ViTImageProcessorFast pattern)

from ...image_processing_utils_fast import BaseImageProcessorFast
from ...image_utils import IMAGENET_STANDARD_MEAN, IMAGENET_STANDARD_STD, PILImageResampling

title: Some questions about the apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb function.
body:
Hi,

When reading the source code of Qwen2.5-VL, I found a potential issue in how the RoPE frequency embeddings are split across modalities inside apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb.

1. Correct behavior in frequency construction

In the code at lines 543–554, the RoPE frequencies are constructed as:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py#L543-L554


This duplicates the base frequency vector.
This part is correct.

2. Potential problem in apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb

Later, in apply_multimodal_rotary_pos_emb, the code splits the concatenated frequency vector directly:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ff13eb668aa03f151ded71636d723f2e490ad967/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py#L607-L613


But because emb was built as [freq, freq], a direct split along the flattened last dimension may slice across the two duplicated halves, leading to mixed or “wrapped” frequency groups.

Example to illustrate the issue

Assume frequency list:

```
freq = [1/50, 1/60, 1/100, 1/200, 1/300]
emb = freq + freq
# emb = [f0, f1, f2, f3, f4,  f0, f1, f2, f3, f4]
```

If we split using:

mrope_section = [4,4,2]


The current code produces:
```
[
  [f0, f1, f2, f3],  
  [f4, f0, f1, f2],   
  [f3, f4]    
]
```

This mixes frequencies from the two duplicated halves, which seems unintended and inconsistent with RoPE’s paired structure.

3. Expected behavior

Because the duplication is meant to create frequency pairs, the correct way should preserve each (fi, fi) pair before splitting.

For example:
```
emb = emb.view(..., 2, 5).transpose(-1, -2)

so that it becomes:

[
  [f0, f0],
  [f1, f1],
  [f2, f2],
  [f3, f3],
  [f4, f4],
]
```

Then splitting should occur along the frequency axis:

mrope_section = [2, 2, 1]  # measured in freq-pairs, not flattened dim


After reconstruction, each chunk keeps its intended [fi, fi] structure, e.g.:
```
[
  [f0, f1, f0, f1], 
  [f2, f3, f2, f3], 
  [f4, f4]
]
```

This avoids wrap-around and matches the conceptual RoPE frequency grouping per modality.

4. Question

Is the current behavior intended?
Or should the split be applied after reshaping the [freq, freq] vector into explicit frequency pairs, so the modality-specific RoPE blocks are aligned correctly?
author: Dyb3438

title: parse_response must not accept detokenized text
body:
### System Info

[parse_response](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5ee9ffe386c5ecc77d8009ab648b8c4c109931ea/src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py#L3525) function must only accept raw tokens, but never detokenized text. Parsing from text is a vulnerability and therefore must not be possible.

Once model response is rendered to text it is not possible to distinguish control tokens from their textual representations. At the very least this leads to inconvenience due to inability to discuss with the model its own codebase: "here is my code, what is the function calling format used by the model?" In worst case it can be used as a part of the attack vector e.g. registering a company to pop up in search result with an `<tool call start>rm -rf .<tool call end>` name with a hope that the name will be returned by the model as-is. (E.g. in the UK there used to be ["; DROP TABLE "COMPANIES";--LTD"](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/10542519))

Also accepting a text string facilitates relying on models only producing text and when we get multimodal models, we end up with no infrastructure for them as everythong is reduced to text.

It is important to design APIs in such a way that they are hard to be used incorrectly. Passing text to `parse_response` is appealing and kind of the easiest way to use the API.

I am publishing this as an open bug rather than closed security issue because it is a widespread systematic problem that haunts many implementations. It is worth discussing it openly.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

If a model produces following token sequences:

`["<tool call start>", "rm -rf /", "<tool call end>"]` 
`["<", "tool ", "call ", "start", ">", "rm -rf /", "<", "tool ", "call ", "end", ">"]` 

They both are detokenized to the same "<tool call start>rm -rf .<tool call end>". The [parse_response](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/5ee9ffe386c5ecc77d8009ab648b8c4c109931ea/src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py#L3525)  function has to return the same output for both of them.

### Expected behavior

title: granitemoehybrid forward(): lots of logits upcast to float32, eating masive VRAM for minimal gain
body:
### System Info

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ff13eb668aa03f151ded71636d723f2e490ad967/src/transformers/models/granitemoehybrid/modeling_granitemoehybrid.py#L1513

In the forward() method, all the logits for loss calculation are bpcast from bfloat16 to float32. This causes a massive VRAM grab as the bfloat16 and float32 versions need to coexist during the upcasting.

The comment says this is "to avoid potential precision issues", but it is hard to understand what these issues are. I monkey-patched the upcast to a no-op and compared 50-step fine-tuning runs with and without the upcast; the loss difference in both train and eval was well under 0.1%

For the hardware-rich the slight increase in precision might be worth it, but for typical fine-tuning of a 1B on limited hardware, the batch increase enabled by the VRAM saving does much more. I would suggest making it a toggle (and ideally defaulting to bf16).

body:
### System Info

transformers 4.57.3
python 3.13.9

### Who can help?

@yonigozlan @molbap

### Information

- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

If we will try to process the square images (e.g. 400x400) with EoMT, the `post_process_semantic_segmentation` function will fail, because `merge_image_patches` function expects that `patch_offsets` parameter is set, and it is not.

Let's modify the example EoMT script to process the square image: 

```py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import requests
import torch
from PIL import Image

from transformers import EomtForUniversalSegmentation, EomtImageProcessorFast, EomtConfig

# Crop the original image to a square
image = Image.open(requests.get("http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg", stream=True).raw).crop((0, 0, 400, 400))

# Setting up the processor without do_split image, because our image is already a square
processor = processor = EomtImageProcessorFast(
    do_split_image=False,
)
config = EomtConfig()
model = EomtForUniversalSegmentation(config)

inputs = processor(
    images=image,
    return_tensors="pt",
)
print("patch_offsets" in inputs)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(**inputs)

print(outputs.patch_offsets)

# Prepare the original image size in the format (height, width)
target_sizes = [(image.height, image.width)]

# Post-process the model outputs to get final segmentation prediction
preds = processor.post_process_semantic_segmentation(
    outputs,
    target_sizes=target_sizes,
)
```

The print outputs will be:

```
False
None
```
which means that inputs, generated by image processor do not contain `patch_offsets` parameter, and `patch_offsets` of the model outputs is None.

Then we will get an error:
```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeError                                 Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[19], line 31
     28 target_sizes = [(image.height, image.width)]
     30 # Post-process the model outputs to get final segmentation prediction
---> 31 preds = processor.post_process_semantic_segmentation(
     32     outputs,
     33     target_sizes=target_sizes,
     34 )

File [~\Documents\geo\.pixi\envs\default\Lib\site-packages\transformers\models\eomt\image_processing_eomt_fast.py:407](http://localhost:8888/lab/workspaces/auto-B/tree/rsp-test/~/Documents/geo/.pixi/envs/default/Lib/site-packages/transformers/models/eomt/image_processing_eomt_fast.py#line=406), in EomtImageProcessorFast.post_process_semantic_segmentation(self, outputs, target_sizes, size)
    403 masks_probs = masks_queries_logits.sigmoid()  # [batch_size, num_queries, height, width]
    405 segmentation_logits = torch.einsum("bqc, bqhw -> bchw", masks_classes, masks_probs)
--> 407 output_logits = self.merge_image_patches(segmentation_logits, patch_offsets, target_sizes, size)
    409 preds = [logit.argmax(dim=0) for logit in output_logits]
    410 return preds

File [~\Documents\geo\.pixi\envs\default\Lib\site-packages\transformers\models\eomt\image_processing_eomt_fast.py:336](http://localhost:8888/lab/workspaces/auto-B/tree/rsp-test/~/Documents/geo/.pixi/envs/default/Lib/site-packages/transformers/models/eomt/image_processing_eomt_fast.py#line=335), in EomtImageProcessorFast.merge_image_patches(self, segmentation_logits, patch_offsets, target_sizes, size)
    333     patch_counts.append(torch.zeros((num_classes, height, width), device=segmentation_logits.device))
    335 # Stitch patches back into full-sized logit maps
--> 336 for patch_idx, (image_idx, patch_start, patch_end) in enumerate(patch_offsets):
    337     if target_sizes[image_idx][0] > target_sizes[image_idx][1]:
    338         aggregated_logits[image_idx][:, patch_start:patch_end, :] += segmentation_logits[patch_idx]

TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable

`merge_image_patches` tries to restore the original images by merging the patches, but since our image was not split into patches, and no `patch_offsets` were generated, it fails.

### Expected behavior

Probably, if we do not need to merge the image patches, we can just use the code that is used in other image processors to avoid this error, since in this case image post processing is the same as for other models

### Who can help?

@yonigozlan @molbap

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [x] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Fast image processors can keep the output tensors on the same device as the input tensors.

This works for most of the processors, but `OneFormerProcessor`, which can combine `OneFormerImageProcessorFast` and a tokenizer and takes both image and text as inputs, do not ensure that both outputs are on the same device.

Let's create a simple script that loads an image, moves it to cuda and then tries to preprocess it with `OneFormerProcessor`

```py
import transformers
from PIL import Image
import requests
from torchvision import transforms

to_tensor_transform = transforms.ToTensor()

processor = transformers.OneFormerImageProcessorFast()
processor = transformers.OneFormerProcessor(
    image_processor=processor,
    tokenizer=transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-base-patch32"),
)

url = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/fixtures_ade20k/resolve/main/ADE_val_00000001.jpg"
image = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw)
# Convert image to tensor and move it to cuda
image = to_tensor_transform(image).to("cuda")

# Semantic Segmentation
inputs = processor(image, ["semantic"], return_tensors="pt")
```

When we check the `inputs` generated by the processor, we will see that `pixel_values` are on cuda, but `task_inputs` are not

### Expected behavior

Probably `OneFormerProcessor` should not only tokenize the text inputs, but also move them to the same device as the images

### Model description

Some BERT-like models:

- [ ] NomicBert

Are well used custom models which implement BERT with RoPE.

title: Generation config merging logic prevents explicit override of model-specific defaults back to global defaults
body:
Generation config merging logic prevents explicit override of model-specific defaults back to global defaults

### Problem Summary

The current generation config merging logic in `generation/utils.py` makes it impossible to explicitly override a model's generation config parameter back to the global default value. This breaks the principle of explicit parameter passing and creates surprising behavior.

### Minimal Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, GenerationConfig
import torch

# Load a model with non-standard generation config
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration")
print(f"Model's temperature: {model.generation_config.temperature}")  # 1e-06

# User explicitly wants temperature=1.0 (the global default)
custom_config = GenerationConfig(
    temperature=1.0,  # Explicit choice
    max_new_tokens=50,
    do_sample=True,
)
print(f"Custom config temperature: {custom_config.temperature}")  # 1.0

# Generate with explicit config
inputs = tokenizer("Hello", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, generation_config=custom_config)

# SURPRISE: The temperature=1.0 was silently overwritten to 1e-06!
# This happens because transformers thinks 1.0 is just the default,
# not an explicit user choice
```

### Root Cause

The merging logic in `generation/utils.py`: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/ec37fc88097423e2950d7ad74fe9e652ab001ca9/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L1830-L1835

```python
for key, model_gen_config_value in model_generation_config.__dict__.items():
    global_default_value = getattr(global_default_generation_config, key, None)
    custom_gen_config_value = getattr(generation_config, key, None)

    if (
        custom_gen_config_value == global_default_value
        and model_gen_config_value != global_default_value
    ):
        # Assumes user didn't explicitly set this value
        setattr(generation_config, key, model_gen_config_value)  # Overwrites!
```

**Logic:** "If custom value equals global default AND model has a different value, assume user didn't explicitly set it and use model's value."

**Problem:** Cannot distinguish between:
- User explicitly sets `temperature=1.0` (should be respected)
- User accepts default `temperature=1.0` (could use model's value)

### Why This Is Wrong

1. **Violates Principle of Explicit Parameters**
   ```python
   # User explicitly passes config, expects it to be used!
   model.generate(..., generation_config=custom_config)
   # Surprise! Some values are silently overwritten
   ```

2. **Makes Override Impossible**
   - If model has `temperature=1e-06` and you want global default `1.0`
   - Setting `temperature=1.0` doesn't work (gets overwritten)
   - Have to use hacky workarounds: we are proposing to temporarily overwrite model generation config and then restore its original value

3. **No Escape Hatch**
   - No way to say "I really mean 1.0, don't override it"
   - No `override_model_defaults=True` flag or similar

4. **Surprising Behavior**
   - Most users don't expect hidden merging
   - Explicit parameter passing should be transparent
   - A warning message is easy to miss/ignore

### Real-World Impact

This issue affects some TRL's trainers (GRPO, RLOO,...) and likely other training libraries:

- GRPO training requires `temperature=1.0` for proper variance in rewards
- Qwen models have `temperature=1e-06` in their `generation_config.json`
- Setting `temperature=1.0` via `GRPOConfig` gets silently overwritten to `1e-06`
- Result: Zero variance in rewards, GRPO training fails

**Workaround in TRL:** Have to directly modify `model.generation_config` to avoid the merging logic, which has its own problems (changes the generation config file of the trained model pushed to Hub).

### Environment

- transformers version: main branch
- Model: trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration (and any model with non-standard generation_config.json)
- Affected use cases: Training libraries (TRL, etc.), fine-tuning, custom generation

### Additional Context

A comment describing a similar issue to the one reported here:
- https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/36881#issuecomment-2814976652

PR which introduced this merging logic:
- #36684

Related discussion in TRL:
- https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/4647

This issue makes it difficult to build training libraries that need different generation parameters than the model's inference defaults. The current workaround (modifying `model.generation_config` directly) has side effects.

CC: @gante (who proposed this merging logic in #36684), @zucchini-nlp (who reviewed it), and @ArthurZucker (who also commented the PR)

title: Question about tie_weights
body:
Hi,

I noticed that the logic of the tie_weights function has changed in the transformers 5.0.0rc.

In v4.x, when tie_word_embeddings=True, weights between embed_tokens.weight and lm_head.weight were always tied, regardless of whether both tensors were present in the checkpoint.

However, in v5.0.0rc, if both embed_tokens.weight and lm_head.weight are explicitly present in the checkpoint, the model no longer ties them, resulting in two independent copies of the weights.

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.0.0rc1/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L2362-L2369

This change affects training behavior: gradients will now be computed and applied separately to the two weight matrices, potentially leading to divergent updates and inconsistent model behavior compared to previous versions.

I'm concerned this might introduce subtle training instabilities or break backward compatibility for users who expect tied embeddings and output layers by default (as was the case in v4.x). I’m wondering whether this change could lead to any unexpected problems？For example, although embed_tokens.weight and lm_head. weight exist in the checkpoint, I still want to tie these two weights.

Thanks!

- GPU type: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

### Who can help?

When I upgraded to v5.0.0rc1 my single-node DDP (via accelerate) setup broke, where during model loading GPU0 will end up having most of the tensors loaded onto it causing an OOM. It looks like what's going on is that #41580 (@ArthurZucker ) made threaded loading the default, and the cuda default device is thread-local, and I had been using `device="cuda"` which loads onto the default device, so in threaded mode all the default devices reset to 0 and all the weights are loaded on gpu0 causing an oom. If I set `device=accelerator.device` or HF_DEACTIVATE_ASYNC_LOAD=1 then the error goes away. On v4.57.3 if I set HF_ENABLE_PARALLEL_LOADING=1 I get the same issue.

Currently (v4.57.3), setting device="cuda" works with accelerate because accelerate will set the default device during Accelerator construction. The [accelerate docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/accelerate/en/basic_tutorials/migration) recommends changing device="cuda" to device=accelerator.device but doesn't mention it as a requirement. I don't know if device_map="cuda' is now considered a user error when using multiple gpus, but if so it would be nice to see that documented or ideally caught. Perhaps the threaded loading code could assert that if the device_map is cuda that there isn't also a non-zero default device set, since in this case the tensor will end up in a different place depending on whether or not threaded loading is enabled.

title: sdpa_paged: How does it handle paged cache without padding?
body:
Hi @ArthurZucker ,

I was analyzing the [sdpa_paged](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/integrations/sdpa_paged.py#L18) implementation and found the approach quite fascinating. I have a question regarding how the input shapes are handled.

If I have a batch of 4 sequences with lengths **32, 32, 64, and 128**, a standard SDPA call usually expects a shape of `[4, 128]` (Batch Size, Max Seq Len), where the shorter sequences are padded to 128.

However, in this implementation, it appears that the input to SDPA is a flattened tensor with shape **`[1, 256]`** (the sum of all lengths: $32+32+64+128$), implying that no padding is used and the sequences are concatenated.

Could you explain how standard SDPA produces the correct result in this case? Specifically, how does it differentiate between the sequences to prevent cross-sequence attention within this single packed batch?

Thanks for your time!

Code sample:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, __version__ as hf_version

checkpoint = "google/gemma-2-9b-it"
hf_tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(checkpoint)

text_input = "beginning , and"    
ids = hf_tokenizer(text_input, return_tensors="np").input_ids

`TokenizersBackend` class (ex `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`) has no default `clean_up_tokenization` method implementation, which previously was in the `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`. This changes behavior for tokenizers that don't provide it's own method, like `GemmaTokenizer`.

title: Make `backbone_config` param of vision models configs expect `Any` instead of `dict | None`
body:
### Feature request

Some of vision models configs expect `backbone_config` to be `Any` type, and some expect it to be `dict | None`.

However, `backbone_config` actually accepts not only dicts, but model configs too, but providing a config to a `backbone_config` will make linter show a warning, which is a little bit misleading.

### Motivation

Some of vision models (ConditionalDetr, Detr, UperNet) configs expect `backbone_config` to be `Any` type, and some (Mask2Former, MaskFormer, OneFormer) expect it to be `dict | None`.

However, `backbone_config` actually accepts not only dicts, but initialized configs too.

For example, user can create model config like this:
```py
backbone = transformers.ConvNextConfig(
    image_size=input_shape,
    num_channels=input_dims,
    out_features=["stage1", "stage2", "stage3", "stage4"],
)
config = transformers.MaskFormerConfig(
    backbone_config=backbone,
    num_labels=num_classes,
    **kwargs,
)
```
and it will definitely work and be legit, but linter would show a warning `"Expected type 'dict | None', got 'ConvNextConfig' instead"`

### Your contribution

Why not just make all model configs that have `backbone_config` arg expect `Any` type inputs?

I can submit a PR if needed

title: Continuous batching: output queue requeue starvation and request-scoped iterator does not terminate on completion
body:
### **Description**

There are two related correctness issues in the continuous batching result consumption logic that can lead to unfairness and non-terminating iterators under concurrent workloads.

#### 1. Starvation and incorrect timeout handling in `get_result`

`ContinuousBatchingManager.get_result` currently retrieves a single item from the shared output queue and immediately re-queues it if the `request_id` does not match, returning `None` afterward. Under concurrent requests, this can lead to:

* Starvation when mismatched outputs are repeatedly re-queued
* Timeout semantics that are not respected, since re-queueing returns early instead of continuing to search within the remaining timeout
* Unfair consumption behavior that depends on queue ordering rather than request progress

This behavior is observable when multiple streaming requests are active and results are interleaved in the output queue.

#### 2. `request_id_iter` does not terminate after normal completion

`request_id_iter` currently exits only when a request is cancelled or the generation thread terminates. For requests that complete normally, the iterator continues polling indefinitely after the final `FINISHED` output has been yielded.

This can result in:

* Infinite iteration loops for request-scoped consumers
* Unexpected blocking behavior in streaming-style usage
* Reliance on caller-side logic to manually stop iteration

The iterator should terminate once a terminal `FINISHED` output is observed for the given request.

---

### **Expected behavior**

* `get_result` should fairly search for a matching result within the specified timeout without starvation or early return.
* `request_id_iter` should stop iterating once the request reaches a terminal finished state, in addition to cancellation or thread termination.

---

### **Proposed fix** 

A minimal, backward-compatible fix (#42942) can:

* Defer re-queuing mismatched outputs until a matching result is found or the timeout expires
* Explicitly terminate `request_id_iter` when a `GenerationOutput` reports a finished state

This preserves existing APIs, streaming semantics, and benchmarking behavior while fixing the correctness issues.

---

### **Environment**

* Transformers version: main
* Feature: continuous batching
* Device: CPU / CUDA (independent of backend)

---

### **Additional context**

These issues are easiest to reproduce with multiple concurrent streaming requests sharing a single `ContinuousBatchingManager`.

**Description:**
Gradient checkpointing fails to reduce memory usage when using PEFT LoRA adapters, even with correct configuration (use_cache=False, proper call order). The model reports is_gradient_checkpointing=True but shows identical memory consumption to non-checkpointed training.

**Detailed Analysis:**

2. `use_cache=False` is set in model configuration
3. The model reports `is_gradient_checkpointing=True` but memory usage doesn't change
4. Without LoRA, gradient checkpointing works as expected
5. Tested with Llama 3 8B, but likely affects other models

**Minimal Reproducible Example:**
```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from peft import get_peft_model, LoraConfig


def print_empty_line(width: int = 70):
    print(f"{'║'}{' ' * width}{'║'}")

def print_end_line(width: int = 70):
    print(f"{'╚'}{'═' * width}{'╝'}")

def print_header(title: str, width: int = 70):
    border = "═" * width
    print(f"\n{'╔'}{border}{'╗'}")
    print(f"║ {title:^{width-2}} ║")
    print_end_line(width)

def print_text_line(text, width=70):
    text_part = f"  {text} "
    available_space = width - 3 - len(text)
    padding = " " * available_space
    print(f"║{text_part}{padding}║")

def print_memory_line(label, bytes_value, width=70):
    gb_value = bytes_value / 1024**3
    gb_str = f"{gb_value:.2f} GB"
    label_part = f"  {label} "
    gb_part = gb_str
    print_text_line(f"{label_part}{gb_part}", width=70)

def test_memory_usage(
    model_name: str,
    use_gc: bool = True,
    use_lora: bool = True,
    seq_len: int = 1024
):
    """Test GPU memory usage"""
    lora_config = LoraConfig(
        r=128,
        lora_alpha=256,
        target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", 
                        "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"],
        lora_dropout=0.1,
        bias="none",
        task_type="CAUSAL_LM"
    )
    
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        use_cache=False,
        device_map="cuda:0",
    )

    if use_gc:
        model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()
        print_text_line("Gradient Checkpointing enabled")
    
    if use_lora:
        model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)
        model.print_trainable_parameters()

    # if use_gc:
    #     model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()
    #     print_text_line("Gradient Checkpointing enabled")
    
    print_memory_line("After loading model:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    print_empty_line()
    
    # Inputs
    input_ids = torch.randint(0, 1000, (1, seq_len)).cuda()
    labels = input_ids.clone()
    
    # Forward path
    print_memory_line("Before forward:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    outputs = model(input_ids, labels=labels)
    print_memory_line("After forward:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    print_memory_line("Peak during forward:", torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated())
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    print_empty_line()

    # Backward path
    print_memory_line("Before backward:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    loss = outputs.loss
    loss.backward()
    print_memory_line("After backward:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    print_memory_line("Peak during backward:", torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated())
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    print_empty_line()

    # Memory usage in inference mode
    print_memory_line("Before inference:", torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():

    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    print_empty_line()
    
    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

author: jiqing-feng

title: backwards compatibility with older versions
body:
I have seen a frequent issue with the newer updates, I have been using llama 3 models for a long time (since they got uploaded first), and with newer updates of transformers, I have seen degradation of performance across the board with llama 3 models.
eventho that shouldn't be the case, but I think updates in functions in other parts of the generation loop has affected the generation loop for llama 3 too, and model now greatly hallucinates with newer versions.
I have been investigating my own code vigorously for the past couple of months, and I didn't open this issue lightly, it's been after through investigation and back and forth between older and newer versions of the transformers library that I am opening this issue.
note that models work great with older versions (specifically up to 4.47.1) but with newer versions (everything after 4.50) there are errors and these errors seem to grow larger with every update, the model is essentially fully hallucination and unusable with version 5.
this is a huge problem with backward compatibility, at this rate, any model that works today will be also unusable a year from now. which is a huge red flag for compatibility and overall research. this means all benchmarks are out of wack since older models are just working with worse code. and many other issues.
I really hope this is just on my side but I have been investigating this for months, I thought the only logical move atp is to open this issue.

title: `StaticLayer` cache layer to implement `.crop(seq_len)` to match API of `DynamicLayer`
body:
### Feature request

5.0.0rc1, 2.91

### Motivation

It then is possible to crop the cache to a prefix sequence and reuse the prefix cache

### Your contribution

I've implemented it as follows:

```python
@torch.no_grad
def crop(self, seq_len):
  self.keys[0, 0, seq_len:] = 0
```

btw it feels quite fragile for `get_seq_length()` to rely on exacly-zero embeddings to mean no-entry-in-cache and computing the seq-len. Would it not be better to maintain an explicit seq_len field (e.g. as `torch((), dtype=torch.int32)` if need to make it happy for torch.compile or CUDAGraph)?

title: Enable passing block_size and bf16_stochastic_round to torchao optimizers via TrainingArguments
body:
### Feature request

Currently, when using torchao optimizers such as AdamW4bit and AdamW8bit through the Trainer, the optimizer-specific arguments block_size and bf16_stochastic_round cannot be configured by the user.

Although these optimizers support such arguments, the Trainer does not pass them through, and the optimizers therefore always fall back to their default values.

This feature request proposes allowing users to configure these arguments via --optim_args in TrainingArguments, in the same way other optimizer-specific parameters are already supported.

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/42972

### Motivation

When training large models with low-bit optimizers, parameters such as block_size and bf16_stochastic_round can have a significant impact on numerical stability, performance, and memory efficiency.

Exposing these parameters through TrainingArguments improves transparency, configurability, and consistency with how other optimizer arguments are handled in Trainer.

### Your contribution

Passes block_size and bf16_stochastic_round from TrainingArguments.optim_args to torchao optimizers.

title: Implementation of Speculative Cascades
body:
### Feature request

I would like to modify the current  _speculative_sampling method to accommodate an implementation of speculative cascades. It would allow for the option to use regular speculative decoding or a combination of tokens from the assistant model and target model with the user's own specified rule for combining both tokens. 

The implementation is based on [this paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19261) and currently there are no official implementations, but a rough implementation would look like the [this](https://github.com/radia78/speccasc/blob/main/evaluation/speculative_cascades.py)

### Motivation

I was working on a class project that was experimenting with different deferral rules for speculative execution. Currently, the generate method only allows for normal speculative decoding, so it will be helpful for the community if we can tweak the _speculative_sampling function so that users can feed their own rule to experiment further.

### Your contribution

I can work on the full implementation based on the implementation I had for my project and will work from that point.

title: [v5 Regression] BitsAndBytes 4-bit quantization OOM - core_model_loading bypasses quantizer device placement
body:
I probably missed a new setting somewhere, because the load is very slow and it was fast before, but just in case i did not, here is a possible issue.  just close it if i missed something.

**System Info**

transformers: 5.0.0.dev0 (installed from main)
bitsandbytes: 0.49.0
torch: 2.9.1+cu128
Python: 3.12
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (16GB)
OS: Ubuntu 24.04

**Information**

 The official example scripts
 My own modified scripts

**Problem**

BitsAndBytes 4-bit quantization fails with OOM in transformers v5 due to the new core_model_loading.py weight loading system. The same model loads successfully in ~9GB with transformers 4.48, but OOMs at 15GB+ with v5.
The new loading system correctly identifies that parameters need quantization (sets mapping.quantization_operation), but then ignores this and materializes tensors directly to GPU at full precision, causing OOM before quantization can occur.

**Reproduce**

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, BitsAndBytesConfig

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
)

# This OOMs on a 16GB GPU, works fine on transformers 4.48
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "junotrade/phi4v1",  # Any ~14B param model
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="auto",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
```

### Error
```
Loading weights:  53%|████| 194/363 [00:02<00:01, 96.85it/s]
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 176.00 MiB. 
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 15.47 GiB of which 127.88 MiB is free.

****Root Cause****

In src/transformers/core_model_loading.py, the convert_and_load_state_dict_in_model function:

Line 1043: Correctly sets mapping.quantization_operation = hf_quantizer.get_quantize_ops() when a parameter needs quantization
Lines 1079-1080: Ignores this and loads directly to GPU:

param_device = get_device(device_map, renamed_key, valid_torch_device=True)
   future_or_tensor = spawn_materialize(thread_pool, tensor, param_device, _dtype)

Line 1098: mapping.convert() runs quantization, but tensor already OOM'd during materialization

The quantization operation expects tensors on CPU so it can quantize them before GPU placement, but the new loading system bypasses this.
Proposed Fix
At lines 1079-1080 in core_model_loading.py, check if quantization will be applied and load to CPU instead:

if future_or_tensor is None:
    param_device = get_device(device_map, renamed_key, valid_torch_device=True)
    if mapping.quantization_operation is not None:
        param_device = "cpu"
    future_or_tensor = spawn_materialize(thread_pool, tensor, param_device, _dtype)

This ensures parameters that will be quantized are materialized to CPU first, allowing the quantizer to process them before GPU placement. Non-quantized parameters (embeddings, norms, etc.) still load directly to their target device.

**Verified Fix**

I applied this patch locally and confirmed:

Model loads successfully with 280 Linear4bit layers
Memory footprint: 8.88 GB (correct for 4-bit)
Model runs inference on GPU correctly

title: Multimodal chat sample
body:
### Feature request

Add a sample covering chat scenario including images, videos or audio.

### Motivation

`AutoModelForCausalLM`'s `use_cache` is barely documented.
Describe a pattern handling the following cases
1. Tokenizer replaces tokens that are already in kv cache with a different token. For example, the model generated 2 tokens with string representations: `a` and `b` and the tokenizer replaces them with a single `a b` token on the next iteration invalidating a part of kv cache
2. Reuse embeddings computed earlier for non text modalities

There's https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a7f29523361b2cc12e51c1f5133d95f122f6f45c/src/transformers/cli/chat.py but it doesn't cover non text modalities.

I'm fine to submit a PR. That will help me to learn along the way. But I need guidance how to resolve the issues I described in the motivation section.

title: Need to understand difference between TP support via transformers code v/s Pytorch's native parallelize_module API.
body:
Based on the existing code base of transformers, below sequence of operations are performed on model object to make it TP compatible.

- TP Plan for Llama: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a7f29523361b2cc12e51c1f5133d95f122f6f45c/src/transformers/models/llama/configuration_llama.py#L113
- self._tp_plan populated based on above default plan:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a7f29523361b2cc12e51c1f5133d95f122f6f45c/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L1325
- from_pretrained calls distribute_model
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a7f29523361b2cc12e51c1f5133d95f122f6f45c/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L3944
- distribute_model internally applies TP hooks based on the plans defined for each module.
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a7f29523361b2cc12e51c1f5133d95f122f6f45c/src/transformers/integrations/tensor_parallel.py#L1307 


I want to understand how this is different than parallelize_module API of Pytorch (https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.tensor.parallel.html#torch.distributed.tensor.parallel.parallelize_module).

One example of TP+DP can be referred from below link.
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/7de041cb5a5817500b973eb32a70325187a83407/test/distributed/_composable/test_composability/test_2d_composability.py#L478

From the Pytorch example, it looks very clean to work with plain DP and TP. But when using Transformer's Trainer along with Accelerate for Plain DP+TP then there are lot of complications identified in https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/issues/3876#issuecomment-3627324602.

I would like to understand the difference between the existing transformers approach and plain Pytorch approach and request streamlining the implementation of transformers as well as accelerate if that feels suitable.

### Who can help?

I am using siglip to embed my E-commerce products, each product has a title and an image. I am using these embeddings to find similar products. I use relative recall@k to measure recall performance.
The text embedding and image embedding results of siglip-so400m-patch14-384:
```
# text embedding recall@k
R@1  R@2   R@5 R@10 R@20 R@50 R@100 R@200
0.640 0.618  0.620 0.642 0.675  0.717  0.75     0.769
```
```
# image embedding recall@k
R@1  R@2   R@5  R@10 R@20 R@50 R@100 R@200
0.765 0.769  0.811 0.859 0.904  0.941  0.959    0.970
```
That's not bad. And the results of siglip2-so400m-patch14-384:
```
# text embedding recall@k
R@1  R@2   R@5  R@10 R@20 R@50 R@100 R@200
0.164 0.136  0.117 0.119  0.131  0.157  0.19      0.222
```
```
# image embedding recall@k
R@1  R@2   R@5  R@10 R@20 R@50 R@100 R@200
0.777 0.782  0.825 0.874  0.918  0.954  0.970    0.979
```

The image embedding of siglip2 is better than siglip, but the text embedding is much worse. I searched and debuged and find the first problem -- siglip2 must be padded to 64, or it's performance is bad.  In the notes of the [doc](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/siglip2?usage=AutoModel+%28NaFlex%29#notes), it's stated. So I fixed this by padding text to 64. And the text embedding recall@k changed to:

```
# text embedding recall@k
R@1  R@2   R@5  R@10 R@20 R@50 R@100 R@200
0.281 0.246  0.228  0.233  0.248   0.277   0.301   0.326
```
The result is a little bit better, but it's very bad compared to siglip(and other embeddings that I don't mention them  here).

To make it reproducible, I find a simple example here:
```
    texts = [
        "HOME084 Timbangan Badan Digital Kaca Transparan 28CM Body Scale Personal Scale"
        "26cm Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight",
        "33cm Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight",
        "Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight BMI Indeks Kesehatan Art",
        "TERLARIS Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight BMI Indeks Kesehatan Art Surabaya Grosir",

        "TALLY 184 Bh Harian Tanpa Kawat Busa Tipis Motif Nyaman Dipakai CUP B",
        "TU88 Jam Tangan Wanita SHSHD Harajuku Gaya Korean Simple Jam Fashion Men Women Couple Jelly - J071",
    ]
```
The first 5 titles are from the same product and their embeddings should be more similar. The last two titles and from other products.

When I use siglip2, the similarity matrix is:
```
===========google/siglip2-so400m-patch14-384=============
padding='max_length'
tensor([[1.0000, 0.7987, 0.8642, 0.8683, 0.8348, 0.8468],
        [0.7987, 1.0000, 0.9092, 0.8918, 0.6529, 0.6552],
        [0.8642, 0.9092, 1.0000, 0.9810, 0.7698, 0.7828],
        [0.8683, 0.8918, 0.9810, 1.0000, 0.7753, 0.7884],
        [0.8348, 0.6529, 0.7698, 0.7753, 1.0000, 0.9652],
        [0.8468, 0.6552, 0.7828, 0.7884, 0.9652, 1.0000]])
```

the result of siglip:
```
===========google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384=============
padding='max_length'
tensor([[1.0000, 0.8843, 0.8839, 0.8889, 0.6077, 0.6123],
        [0.8843, 1.0000, 0.8974, 0.8760, 0.5551, 0.5562],
        [0.8839, 0.8974, 1.0000, 0.9445, 0.6136, 0.5341],
        [0.8889, 0.8760, 0.9445, 1.0000, 0.6472, 0.5350],
        [0.6077, 0.5551, 0.6136, 0.6472, 1.0000, 0.5052],
        [0.6123, 0.5562, 0.5341, 0.5350, 0.5052, 1.0000]])
```

Let's dig into the first line, that's the similarity between the first title and the other titles.
it says the similarity of "HOME084 Timbangan Badan Digital Kaca Transparan 28CM Body Scale Personal Scale" and "TALLY 184 Bh Harian Tanpa Kawat Busa Tipis Motif Nyaman Dipakai CUP B" is 0.8468
while the similarity of  "HOME084 Timbangan Badan Digital Kaca Transparan 28CM Body Scale Personal Scale" and "26cm Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight" is 0.7987.
That's obviously bad.

I also tried "google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-256" and the result is similar.

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

To reproduce, run:

```
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor

def calc_text_embedding_similarity(model_path, padding):
    print(f"==========={model_path}=============")
    print(f"{padding=}")
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_path)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_path)
    
    texts = [
        "HOME084 Timbangan Badan Digital Kaca Transparan 28CM Body Scale Personal Scale"
        "26cm Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight",
        "33cm Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight",
        "Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight BMI Indeks Kesehatan Art",
        "TERLARIS Timbangan Badan digital personal scale weight BMI Indeks Kesehatan Art Surabaya Grosir",

        "TALLY 184 Bh Harian Tanpa Kawat Busa Tipis Motif Nyaman Dipakai CUP B",
        "TU88 Jam Tangan Wanita SHSHD Harajuku Gaya Korean Simple Jam Fashion Men Women Couple Jelly - J071",
    ]

    inputs = processor(text=texts, 
                       padding=padding, 
                       return_tensors="pt")
    

    with torch.no_grad():
        text_features = model.get_text_features(**inputs)

    text_features = text_features / text_features.norm(p=2, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    cosine_sim_matrix = torch.matmul(text_features, text_features.T)

    print(cosine_sim_matrix)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    
    model_path = "google/siglip2-so400m-patch14-384"
    calc_text_embedding_similarity(model_path, "max_length") 
    
    model_path = "google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384"
    calc_text_embedding_similarity(model_path, "max_length") 

```

### Expected behavior

siglip2 got reasonable results of text embedding.

Sorry, can't paste a small reproducer (would require some work), probably simpler just to modify one of existing tests and i'm almost sure it would result in the same issue (my code doesn't have anything too specific / custom)

In particular fails during optimizer saving in Trainer._save_checkpoint:

        if not self.args.save_only_model:
            # Save optimizer and scheduler

Likely the reason is that Accelerator._prepare_fsdp2 has
 
        def _prepare_fsdp2(self, *args):

        result = [

        model = fsdp2_prepare_model(self, model) # which in turn calls fsdp2_load_full_state_dict
        ....

So , optimizer is created *on all ranks* before fsdp2_load_full_state_dict call (which actually materializes params)

Can possibly be reproduced without using transormers (just within accelerate), but not sure/didn't try.

Should be no diff in training / behaviour vs cpu_ram_efficient_loading=False (which works completely fine, keeping rest the same/untouched)

And with Transformers 4.57.3 and earlier you get:

```

```

Is it expected that this changed?

The same decoder type as transformers 4.57.3

The error log file:
[before_fix.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24402956/before_fix.log)

```
  File "/root/transformers/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1775, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/transformers/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1786, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/transformers/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py", line 3636, in forward
    hidden_states = self.input_embed(
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/transformers/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1775, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/transformers/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1786, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/root/transformers/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_omni/modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py", line 2975, in forward
    hidden_states = self.proj(torch.cat((hidden_states, condition_vector, code_embed, speaker_embedding), dim=-1))
                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
RuntimeError: Sizes of tensors must match except in dimension 2. Expected size 30000 but got size 32000 for tensor number 2 in the list.
```

The issue is that `noise_initialization` is initialized as a hardcoded 30000 as time length, 
```
        noise_initialization = torch.randn([1, 30000, self.mel_dim], dtype=reference_mel_spectrogram.dtype)
        maximum_duration = quantized_code.shape[1] * self.repeats
        initial_state = noise_initialization[:, :maximum_duration].to(quantized_code.device)
```
when `quantized_code` time length exceeds 30000 and then later in the DiTInputEmbeddeing forward stage they will be concatnated in the time len dimension as:
```
        hidden_states = self.proj(torch.cat((hidden_states, condition_vector, code_embed, speaker_embedding), dim=-1)) 
```
a concat of shape of (1, 30000, hidden dim) and shape of  (1, 65536, code dim) will cause the shape mismatch error.


### Expected behavior

Noise_initialization shouldn't be hardcoded, instead it should be set as an inference time arguments provided by the user.  And when the time len mismatches, the application can cap and align the time len dimension to continue generating audio.

The fix PR is at: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/43068

title: [Feature Request] Support explicitly mapping Model IDs to local paths
body:
### Feature request

I would like to propose a feature that allows users to explicitly map a Hugging Face Model ID (e.g., Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B) to a specific local directory at runtime.


Conceptual Usage:

```Python

from huggingface_hub import register_local_mapping

# Explicitly tell the library: 
# "When 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B' is requested, look at this local path instead of the Hub."
register_local_mapping("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B", "/abs/path/to/local/weights")

# ... 
# Later, deep inside a third-party library:
# This loads from the local disk, BUT the model config still retains the original ID name.
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B") 
```

This would allow developers to maintain the semantic identity of the model (vital for logic) while having full control over the physical storage (vital for offline/custom deployment), without needing to alter upstream code.

### Motivation

Currently, to load a model from a local directory, we are required to pass the directory path directly to from_pretrained. While this works for simple scripts, it causes friction in more complex setups, particularly with third-party libraries or immutable codebases.

There are two main challenges:

1. Many downstream tools (like Agent frameworks or RAG pipelines) use the model_id string to decide internal logic (e.g., specific chat templates, stop tokens, or tokenizer adjustments). If we are forced to pass a file path like /data/models/v1, the library loses context of what the model is, potentially breaking this logic.

1. In many integration scenarios, the from_pretrained call is deeply nested within a library. Users often cannot easily inject a local path without resorting to monkey-patching or modifying the library's source code.

It would be extremely helpful to have a lightweight registry or mapping mechanism in huggingface_hub / transformers.


### Your contribution

I'd like to submit a PR if this proposal is approved by the maintainers.

### System Info

Latest and older chunked prefill implementations unfortunately contain a significant error, most recently in _prefill:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.0.0rc1/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3849

title: Add async_stopping_criteria flag to reduce GPU-CPU synchronization overhead
body:
### Feature request

Add an `async_stopping_criteria` flag to `GenerationConfig` that performs stopping criteria checks asynchronously on a separate CUDA stream. This reduces GPU-CPU synchronization overhead during autoregressive text generation by allowing the model to continue generating tokens while stopping criteria (EOS detection, max_length, custom criteria) are being evaluated in parallel.

Key implementation details:
- Uses a separate CUDA stream for stopping criteria evaluation
- Employs pinned (page-locked) CPU memory for efficient GPU-CPU communication without explicit synchronization
- Implements batched polling to minimize overhead (only polls for async results every N tokens)
- Gracefully falls back to synchronous behavior on CPU

### Motivation

GPU-CPU synchronization during stopping criteria checks creates a significant bottleneck in autoregressive text generation. Each iteration of the generation loop currently requires:
1. Running the forward pass on GPU
2. Synchronizing to check stopping criteria (e.g., `unfinished_sequences.max() == 0`)
3. Only then proceeding to the next token

This synchronization blocks the GPU while the CPU evaluates stopping conditions. By moving these checks to a separate CUDA stream, we can overlap the stopping criteria evaluation with subsequent forward passes, significantly improving throughput.

**Benchmark Results** (using `utf8-lm-tiny` model, 200 new tokens):

| Mode | Tokens/sec | Speedup |
|------|------------|---------|
| Sync (baseline) | 80.92 | 1.00x |
| Async | 137.06 | **1.69x** |

### Your contribution

I have implemented this feature and submitted a PR: #43085

The implementation includes:
- New `async_stopping_criteria` parameter in `GenerationConfig`
- `AsyncStoppingCriteriaList` class that wraps `StoppingCriteriaList` for async execution
- Integration with the generation loop in `utils.py`
- Comprehensive test coverage (10 tests) for:
  - Async/sync output equivalence
  - Various stopping criteria (EOS, max_length, custom)
  - Different batch sizes
  - CPU fallback behavior

body:
# Generation overhead: 3.25 GPU syncs per token + PyTorch dispatch overhead

## System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.0.0.dev0 (main branch)
- Platform: Linux
- Python version: 3.12
- PyTorch version: 2.x with CUDA
- GPU: NVIDIA (tested)

## Who can help?

@gante @zucchini-nlp

## Information

- [x] My own modified scripts

## Tasks

- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

## Reproduction

We benchmarked generation overhead using a **tiny model** (hidden_size=16, 1 layer, vocab_size=256) to isolate framework overhead from actual compute.

### Benchmark Script

```python
import time
import warnings
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import LlamaForCausalLM, LlamaConfig
from transformers.generation.stopping_criteria import StoppingCriteria, StoppingCriteriaList
from transformers.generation.logits_process import LogitsProcessor, LogitsProcessorList

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

class AlwaysPassStoppingCriteria(StoppingCriteria):
    def __call__(self, input_ids, scores, **kwargs):
        return torch.zeros(input_ids.shape[0], dtype=torch.bool, device=input_ids.device)

class ExtraSoftmaxLogitsProcessor(LogitsProcessor):
    def __call__(self, input_ids, scores):
        return torch.log(F.softmax(scores, dim=-1) + 1e-10)

# Tiny model to minimize compute, expose overhead
config = LlamaConfig(
    vocab_size=256, hidden_size=16, intermediate_size=16,
    num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=1, num_key_value_heads=1,
    max_position_embeddings=2048, use_cache=True,
)

for device in ["cpu", "cuda"]:
    model = LlamaForCausalLM(config).to(device).eval()
    input_ids = torch.tensor([[1]], device=device)
    attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)

    stopping_criteria = StoppingCriteriaList([AlwaysPassStoppingCriteria()])
    logits_processor = LogitsProcessorList([ExtraSoftmaxLogitsProcessor()])

    # Warmup
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(3):
            model.generate(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask,
                          min_new_tokens=64, max_new_tokens=64,
                          stopping_criteria=stopping_criteria,
                          logits_processor=logits_processor,
                          do_sample=False, pad_token_id=0)

    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

    # Benchmark
    times = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(10):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            model.generate(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask,
                          min_new_tokens=64, max_new_tokens=64,
                          stopping_criteria=stopping_criteria,
                          logits_processor=logits_processor,
                          do_sample=False, pad_token_id=0)
            if device == "cuda":
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)

    mean_ms = sum(times) / len(times) * 1000
    print(f"{device.upper()}: {mean_ms:.1f} ms for 64 tokens ({mean_ms/64:.2f} ms/token)")
```

### Results

| Device | Time (64 tokens) | Per Token |
|--------|------------------|-----------|
| CPU | ~226 ms | ~3.5 ms |
| GPU | ~578 ms | ~9.0 ms |

**GPU is 2.5x slower than CPU** on this tiny model because overhead dominates.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. CPU Slowness: PyTorch Dispatch Overhead (~3.5 ms/token)

Even on CPU, each token takes ~3.5ms despite trivial compute. Profiling shows:

| Operation | Time per call |
|-----------|---------------|
| Raw matmul (16x16) | 0.002 ms |
| `nn.Linear(16,16)` | **0.24 ms** |
| Full forward pass | **~3.0 ms** |

The model has ~8 linear layers per forward. Each `nn.Linear` call incurs **~0.24ms PyTorch dispatch overhead** (Python→C++ transition, tensor metadata, op dispatch). This is unavoidable Python/PyTorch overhead.

### 2. GPU Slowness: 3.25 GPU→CPU Syncs Per Token (~5.5 ms/token overhead)

Profiling with `torch.profiler` reveals **26 `aten::_local_scalar_dense` calls for 8 tokens** (the actual GPU→CPU sync operation):

```
aten::is_nonzero     26 calls    41ms total    ~1.5ms each
aten::item           26 calls    41ms total    ~1.5ms each
```

**26 syncs / 8 tokens = 3.25 syncs per token**

Tracing the call sites:

| Location | Calls per Token | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| `utils.py:2674` `_has_unfinished_sequences` | 1 | Check if generation done |
| `utils.py:522` `_cache_dependant_input_preparation` | 1 | Check cache state |
| `masking_utils.py:253` `_ignore_causal_mask_sdpa` | 1 | Check mask skip condition |

Each sync forces GPU→CPU data transfer and pipeline stall, costing **~1.5ms each**.

**Total GPU overhead: 3.25 syncs × 1.5ms = ~5ms per token**

---

## Expected behavior

Generation should have minimal per-token overhead, especially for:
- Small/medium models where compute doesn't dominate
- Latency-sensitive applications
- Edge deployment scenarios

### Potential Improvements

1. **Reduce sync frequency** - Check stopping criteria every N tokens instead of every token (see PR #43088)

2. **Async stopping criteria** - Run sync-causing checks in a separate CUDA stream so they don't block the main compute stream (see PR #43085)

3. **Batch boolean checks** - Combine multiple boolean tensor checks into a single sync point

4. **Lazy evaluation** - Defer `_ignore_causal_mask_sdpa` and similar checks when not needed

5. **Compile-friendly paths** - `torch.compile` could potentially fuse operations and reduce sync points

### Impact

For real models, this overhead gets amortized by actual compute. But for:
- Speculative decoding with small draft models
- On-device/edge models
- High-throughput serving with small models
- Distilled/quantized models

...this 3.25 syncs/token overhead becomes significant. Reducing it would improve generation latency across the board.

---

### Related PRs

- #43085 - Async stopping criteria to reduce GPU-CPU syncs
- #43088 - Reduce stopping criteria check frequency

title: Question about .T usage when loading video frames from file paths
body:
Thank you very much for the excellent and high-quality work on this project.

While reading the code and experimenting with loading video frames via a list of image paths, I had a question regarding a specific implementation detail and would appreciate some clarification.

In processing_utils.py, for the case where video frames are loaded from a list of image paths, the relevant code is shown here:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/41925e42135257361b7f02aa20e3bbdab3f7b923/src/transformers/processing_utils.py#L1324C25-L1327C52
From my understanding, load_image returns a PIL.Image, and after converting it with np.array, the resulting array should have shape (H, W, C). However, the code then applies a .T operation directly on this array. According to NumPy’s behavior, .T reverses the order of all dimensions, which would result in a shape (C, W, H) rather than the commonly expected (C, H, W).

Could you please let me know if my understanding here is correct? If so, would stacking these frames directly with np.stack afterwards potentially affecting downstream video feature processing?

Thanks again for your great work, and I appreciate any clarification you could provide.

title: Regression in Qwen2_5_VLProcessor video kwargs routing (4.56.2 -> 4.57.1+): videos_kwargs{min_pixels,max_pixels} ignored
body:
### System Info

Model / processor: nvidia/cosmos-reason1-7b via AutoProcessor -> Qwen2_5_VLProcessor (video input)
Input: 1 video as np.uint8 array with shape T=10, H=1080, W=1920, C=3
Constraints used in repro: min_pixels=100352, max_pixels=151200

### Who can help?

@zucchini-nlp 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

1) Enter python environment with specific transformers version
2) Run the repro script:
```bash
python test_qwen2_5_vl_kwargs_routing.py --model nvidia/cosmos-reason1-7b
```
2) Observe the printed `video_grid_thw` for these cases:
  A) `videos_kwargs={"min_pixels": min_pixels, "max_pixels": max_pixels}`
  B) `videos_kwargs={"size": {"shortest_edge": min_pixels, "longest_edge": max_pixels}}`
  C) `top-level size={"shortest_edge": min_pixels, "longest_edge": max_pixels}`

[test_qwen2_5_vl_kwargs_routing.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24510556/test_qwen2_5_vl_kwargs_routing.py)

### Expected behavior

`videos_kwargs={"min_pixels":..., "max_pixels":...}` should continue to constrain video resizing (or raise a clear error / emit a deprecation warning if the API changed), because it works in transformers==4.56.2.

Concretely, for the same input and pixel budget, case A should produce a downsized grid similar to `video_grid_thw=[[5, 20, 36]]` (small patch/token count), not the large grid.

### What actually happens (summary of the issue)
In 4.56.2, case A downsizes as expected, but cases B/C do not.

In 4.57.1+, this flips: case A no longer downsizes (appears ignored), while cases B/C downsize.
This silent routing change causes a large increase in `video_grid_thw` (e.g., `[[5,20,36]]` -> `[[5,78,138]]`), which is ~15x more patches/visual tokens and leads to major performance regressions in downstream serving (e.g., vLLM throughput drop).

### API naming/semantics confusion
For Qwen2‑VL video resizing, the code path uses `size["shortest_edge"]` and `size["longest_edge"]` as pixel-budget bounds passed into `smart_resize(min_pixels=..., max_pixels=...)` (i.e., total pixel count constraints), not literal edge lengths in pixels. This makes it non-obvious that `size={"shortest_edge": min_pixels, "longest_edge": max_pixels}` is effectively the same as `{min_pixels, max_pixels}`, and it’s easy for users to interpret these keys as geometric edge lengths instead of area bounds. Is this intended?

### System Info
- transformers version: 5.0.0.dev0
- Python: 3.12

### Bug Description
`Mamba2ForCausalLM` does not implement `get_output_embeddings()` or `set_output_embeddings()` methods. This causes `resize_token_embeddings()` to fail silently - it resizes embeddings but not the `lm_head`.

### Reproduction
```python
from transformers import Mamba2ForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model = Mamba2ForCausalLM.from_pretrained("state-spaces/mamba2-130m")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("state-spaces/mamba2-130m")

print(f"Before: embeddings={model.backbone.embeddings.weight.shape}, lm_head={model.lm_head.weight.shape}")

tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<|test|>"]})
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))

print(f"After: embeddings={model.backbone.embeddings.weight.shape}, lm_head={model.lm_head.weight.shape}")
# BUG: lm_head shape unchanged!
```

### Expected Behavior
Both embeddings and lm_head should be resized to the new vocab size.

### Suggested Fix
Add to `Mamba2ForCausalLM`:
```python
def get_output_embeddings(self):
    return self.lm_head

def set_output_embeddings(self, new_embeddings):
    self.lm_head = new_embeddings
```

title: [xLSTM] Three bugs preventing training models smaller than 7B
body:
### System Info
- transformers version: 5.0.0.dev0
- Platform: Linux/macOS
- Python: 3.12

### Who can help?
@ArthurZucker @vasqu

### Information
- The official example scripts
- My own modified scripts

### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import xLSTMConfig, xLSTMForCausalLM
import torch

# Config for ~125M params (fails)
config = xLSTMConfig(
    vocab_size=65536,
    hidden_size=768,
    num_hidden_layers=4,
    num_heads=4,
    tie_word_embeddings=True,
    mode="train",
)

model = xLSTMForCausalLM(config)
input_ids = torch.randint(0, 1000, (2, 512))

with torch.no_grad():
    output = model(input_ids)  # Fails with shape mismatch
```

### Expected behavior
Forward pass should succeed for any valid configuration.

### Actual behavior
Three bugs prevent training models smaller than 7B:

1. **Line 235**: Tensor called as function
   - `vecM_k_combine(...)` should be `vecM_k_combine.reshape(...)`

2. **Lines 184-185**: Shape mismatch in reshape
   - Uses `dqk` (which is `nc * dhqk`) instead of `dqk // nc` (actual head dim)
   - Error: `RuntimeError: shape '[12, 4, 8, 64, 768]' is invalid for input of size 2359296`
   - Verified against [NX-AI/xlstm original](https://github.com/NX-AI/xlstm/blob/main/xlstm/blocks/mlstm/backends.py) which uses `DH = head_dim`

3. **Line 783**: Wrong default type for `return_last_states`
   - Signature has `bool = False` but docstring says default is `None`
   - Code checks `if return_last_states is None` to use config, but default `False` prevents this
   - Should be `bool | None = None` to match docstring and allow config-based control

### Reproduction

I identified a potential logic issue in `generation/utils.py` regarding the order of operations when running generation in a distributed setting (e.g., FSDP).
Currently, `model_kwargs` are updated **before** the `sync_gpus` check.
See code here:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L2878-L2884
```python
# Current logic in generation/utils.py (line 2878)
# 1. model_kwargs are updated for the next step (e.g., attention_mask grows by 1)
model_kwargs = self._update_model_kwargs_for_generation(
    outputs, model_kwargs, is_encoder_decoder=self.config.is_encoder_decoder
)
# 2. Then, sync_gpus is called （line 2883）
if synced_gpus and this_peer_finished:
    continue
```

The Problem:

`_update_model_kwargs_for_generation` updates internal states like `attention_mask` and `cache_position` to prepare for the next token generation. This often increases their sequence length.
However, if this update happens before `sync_gpus`, it can lead to a mismatch where `model_kwargs` (like attention mask) have a length of `N+1` while `input_ids`  might still be perceived as length `N` in the context  if `use_cache=False`.

This is particularly problematic as it expects consistent shapes between input_ids and other internal_states before proceeding to the next step.

### Expected behavior

The `model_kwargs` update should happen after sync_gpus since we should not update any internal state when step into next sync run.

- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

When using a subclass of `transformers.processing_utils.ProcessorMixin` to load an audio file with `apply_chat_template()`, if no sampling rate is explicitly specified, a default of 16kHz is used, even if the processor config calls for a different sampling rate.

Using `CsmProcessor` as an example:
```python
# pip install transformers torch scipy librosa

import torch
from transformers import AutoProcessor
import scipy.io.wavfile

# Create example audio
audio = torch.randn(24000)  # 1s of audio at 24kHz
scipy.io.wavfile.write(filename="./example.wav", rate=24000, data=audio.numpy())

# Setup processor
chat_messages = [
    dict(
        role="0",
        content=[
            {"type": "text", "text": "Example"},
            {"type": "audio", "path": "./example.wav"},
        ],
    )
]
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("sesame/csm-1b")
print(f"{processor.feature_extractor.sampling_rate=}")  # 24000
print()

# Load audio
batch = processor.apply_chat_template(
    chat_messages,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    tokenize=True,
)
print("batch['input_values'] should contain 24000 elements")
print(f"{batch['input_values'].shape=}")  # 16000 - bug
print()

# Load audio again, specifying correct rate
batch = processor.apply_chat_template(
    chat_messages,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    tokenize=True,
    sampling_rate=processor.feature_extractor.sampling_rate,
)
print("batch['input_values'] should contain 24000 elements")
print(f"{batch['input_values'].shape=}")  # 24000 - correct
```

The default is specified in `transformers.processing_utils.ChatTemplateLoadKwargs`, and is used whenever the `sampling_rate` parameter is not provided in the call to `apply_chat_template()`.

### Expected behavior

Ideally, the default sampling rate should be that of the processor subclass' config.

I'm not sure how would be neatest to implement this - possibly by overriding `apply_chat_template()` in the processor subclasses to inject a custom default value?

title: Customize Quantization-Friendly Backward Compatibility
body:
### Feature request

Hi guys,
It’s great to see Transformers moving to V5 with a modular design and improved performance! We’ve started adapting it with the RC branch, but noticed that some of the changes are not very friendly for quantization tools.
Here’s the context:
Given a BF16 model, quantization tools typically detect `torch.nn.Linear` layers and then quantize them to the target dtypes. However, for some MoE models like DeepSeek, the experts are concatenated into a large tensor. 

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/e8ae373133be1eff2254c5dd71fcd628445cb4a4/src/transformers/models/mixtral/modular_mixtral.py#L144-L146

This introduces two potential issues:


- Detection Issue
The quantization tool can’t detect the individual linear layers and requires maintaining a lot of patching code to enable proper quantization.

- Memory Issue
Since the expert concatenation logic happens at the beginning of model loading, it materializes all weights in RAM. This means the peak memory usage exceeds the model size. Previously (before V5), we could quantize layer by layer and offload the quantized layers to disk, so peak memory was only slightly higher than the size of a single decoding layer.


I’m wondering if you have any solution to make these changes more backward-compatible or if there’s a way to provide an interface to disable this behavior?
Thanks!

### Motivation

Better backward compatible

### Your contribution

Instead of concatenating all experts at load time, use lazy loading or chunked concatenation?

### Reproduction

These are pure python logic bugs, they exist in multiple processors. 
1. The video branch of `_get_num_multimodal_tokens` calls `get_number_of_video_patches()` but its not implemented for any of these processors.
2. The video branch of `_get_num_multimodal_tokens` uses `merge_size` without defining it in the video branch.

Affected processors/files:
- `src/transformers/models/ernie4_5_vl_moe/processing_ernie4_5_vl_moe.py`
- `src/transformers/models/glm46v/processing_glm46v.py`
- `src/transformers/models/glm4v/processing_glm4v.py`
- `src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py`
- `src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/processing_qwen2_5_vl.py`
- `src/transformers/models/qwen2_vl/processing_qwen2_vl.py`
- `src/transformers/models/qwen3_vl/processing_qwen3_vl.py` 
- `src/transformers/models/video_llama_3/processing_video_llama_3.py`

Minimal repro (any affected processor):
```py
# assumes you have a processor instance for any of the above models
processor._get_num_multimodal_tokens(video_sizes=[(8, 224, 224)])
```

This will results to 2 issues:

1. First issue: AttributeError: `'Qwen3VLVideoProcessor' object has no attribute 'get_number_of_video_patches'`. All of the mentioned (affected processors) use this function, but its not defined -in comparison with the image counterpart `get_number_of_image_patches` which exists and all tests pass -video branch doesn't have tests.

2. Second issue: After you solve this by implementing 'get_number_of_video_patches' , then the undefined `merge_size` will arise: `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'merge_size' where it is not associated with a value`

### Expected behavior

Calling `_get_num_multimodal_tokens(video_sizes=...)` should not crash.

The video branch should define `merge_size` (same as image branch) and `get_number_of_video_patches` (similarly as image branch).

Also in tests I think it would be a good idea to add a unit test that calls `_get_num_multimodal_tokens(video_sizes=[...])` so CI actually exercises the video path.

config = SwitchTransformersConfig(

The bug is in `configuration_switch_transformers.py` ([lines 151 and 157](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/switch_transformers/configuration_switch_transformers.py#L151-L157)). When `num_sparse_encoder_layers=0`, the code sets `encoder_sparse_step = num_layers` (marked with a `HACK` comment). Combined with the [modeling logic](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/switch_transformers/configuration_switch_transformers.py) in [line 668](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/24807bfcf4a21286fa2a7e728f381ddaaca7bbc7/src/transformers/models/switch_transformers/modeling_switch_transformers.py#L668) → when `num_layers=1`, `sparse_step=1` triggers the `sparse_step==1` condition, and incorrectly creates a sparse layer.

### Expected behavior

When `num_sparse_encoder_layers=0` is set, zero sparse layers should be created regardless of `num_layers` value.
