- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

1. Install the latest version of transformers
2. Install FlashAttention2
3. Run the provided code
4. Downgrade to transformers version 5.2.0
5. Run the code again

```python
from transformers import Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, AutoProcessor
import torch

model = Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking",
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",
).to("cuda")

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking")

messages = [
    [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "video", "video": torch.zeros(768, 3, 512, 512)},
                {"type": "text", "text": "placeholder"},
            ],
        }
    ],
    [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "video", "video": torch.zeros(768, 3, 512, 512)},
                {"type": "text", "text": "different placeholder"},
            ],
        }
    ],
]

inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=True,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    do_sample_frames=False,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    padding=True,
    padding_side="left",
).to("cuda")

MAX_LEN = 16 * 1024

while True:
    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)

    start.record()
    out_ids = model.generate(
        **inputs, do_sample=False, min_length=MAX_LEN, max_length=MAX_LEN, use_cache=True
    )
    end.record()

    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    assert out_ids.size(0) == 2 and out_ids.size(1) == MAX_LEN

    cur_time = start.elapsed_time(end)
    print(cur_time)
```

### Expected behavior

Tested on an NVIDIA RTX 6000 PRO:
- v5.2.0 FA2 = 92 sec
- v5.4.0 FA2 = 108 sec (+17% overhead)
- v5.2.0 SDPA = 136 sec
- v5.4.0 SDPA = 136 sec (no change)

The performance regression seems to occur when the KV cache is sufficiently large, at which point the GPU memory bandwidth has been saturated. Furthermore, it seems to be related with the changes to the FA2 integration layer. It does not seem to be related with the nvidia-cudnn conv kernel performance regression which was fixed in a recent PyTorch version.

body:
## System Info

```

- Platform: macOS-26.5.1-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.9.6
- PyTorch version: 2.8.0
- CUDA available: False
```

## Who can help?

@yonigozlan @molbap (vision models)

## Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

## Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder
- [x] My own task or dataset (see details below)

## Reproduction

```python
from transformers import Swin2SRImageProcessor
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

processor = Swin2SRImageProcessor()

# 1024 is divisible by 8 (the default size_divisor), so no padding should occur
img = Image.fromarray(np.zeros((1024, 1024, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
out = processor(img, return_tensors="pt")
print(out.pixel_values.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 3, 1032, 1032]) — should be [1, 3, 1024, 1024]
```

The root cause is in `image_processing_swin2sr.py` (lines 75–76) and `image_processing_pil_swin2sr.py` (lines 76–77):

```python
# current (wrong) — always pads by a full size_divisor even when already aligned
pad_height = (height // size_divisor + 1) * size_divisor - height
pad_width  = (width  // size_divisor + 1) * size_divisor - width
```

The `+ 1` forces an extra `size_divisor` of padding even when the dimension is already divisible. The model itself (`modeling_swin2sr.py`, line 747) uses the correct formula:

```python
modulo_pad_height = (window_size - height % window_size) % window_size
```

The test file uses the same wrong formula for expected values, so the tests pass silently.

## Expected behavior

For an image whose dimensions are already divisible by `size_divisor`, the processor should apply zero padding. For a 1024×1024 image with the default `size_divisor=8`, `out.pixel_values.shape` should be `torch.Size([1, 3, 1024, 1024])`, not `torch.Size([1, 3, 1032, 1032])`.

title: Clarify Gemma4 vision bidirectional mask behavior for full vs sliding attention
body:
## Description

I noticed a potential mismatch between HuggingFace Transformers' Gemma4 vision bidirectional mask behavior and the official [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main) implementation.

In the official `google/gemma` implementation, `use_bidirectional_attention="vision"` appears to apply the bidirectional image-token mask only to local sliding attention layers. Global/full attention layers remain causal. Also, for local sliding layers, the final mask is intersected with the sliding window, so image-token bidirectional visibility does not bypass the sliding-window boundary.

In Transformers, `block_sequence_ids` is passed into `create_masks_for_generate(...)`, and then applied to both `full_attention` and `sliding_attention` masks through `blockwise_overlay(...)`.

This seems to result in:

```text
Transformers:
  full_attention = causal OR vision_blockwise_overlay
  sliding_attention = sliding_causal OR vision_blockwise_overlay

Official google/gemma:
  full/global = causal
  local_sliding = (causal OR vision_bidirectional) AND sliding_window
```

This creates two observable differences:

1. In Transformers, full attention layers allow bidirectional visibility inside the image token block, while official `google/gemma` keeps full/global layers causal.
2. In Transformers, image tokens inside the same block can attend bidirectionally across the sliding-window boundary, because the blockwise overlay is OR'ed after the sliding causal mask.

## Relevant Transformers code

In Transformers, Gemma4 constructs `block_sequence_ids` for `use_bidirectional_attention="vision"`:

```python
if self.config.get_text_config().use_bidirectional_attention == "vision":
    block_sequence_ids = torch.full([*inputs_embeds.size()[:-1]], -1, device=inputs_embeds.device)
    if mm_token_type_ids is not None:
        block_sequence_ids = get_block_sequence_ids_for_mask(
            mm_token_type_ids, device=inputs_embeds.device
        )

    mask_kwargs["block_sequence_ids"] = block_sequence_ids

causal_mask_mapping = create_masks_for_generate(**mask_kwargs)
```

Then `create_masks_for_generate(...)` applies the same `block_sequence_ids` to all layer patterns:

```python
for layer_pattern in layer_patterns:
    causal_masks[layer_pattern] = LAYER_PATTERN_TO_MASK_FUNCTION_MAPPING[layer_pattern](**mask_kwargs)
```

Both `create_causal_mask(...)` and `create_sliding_window_causal_mask(...)` apply:

```python
mask_factory_function = or_masks(mask_factory_function, blockwise_overlay(block_sequence_ids))
```

## Reference implementation: google-deepmind/gemma

From [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main), checked locally at commit `ab5a660`.

The Gemma4 config explicitly documents the intended split between sliding and global layers:

```python
# Bidirectional attention for image tokens in the text backbone.
# None: purely causal for all layers (used by E2B, E4B).
# 'vision': bidirectional for image tokens in sliding layers only,
#   causal for global layers (used by 26B_A4B, 31B).
use_bidirectional_attention: str | None = None
```

Source: `gemma/gm/nn/gemma4/_config.py` in [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main).

The transformer creates the normal causal `attention_mask`, and creates a separate `sliding_attention_mask` only when `use_bidirectional_attention == 'vision'`:

```python
if attention_mask is None:
  attention_mask = (
      _attention_mask.make_causal_bidirectional_attention_mask(
          inputs_mask,
          bidirectional_mask=None,
      )
  )

# For models with use_bidirectional_attention='vision' (26B_A4B/31B),
# create a separate sliding attention mask with bidirectional attention
# for image tokens within the same image block.
sliding_attention_mask = None
if self.config.use_bidirectional_attention == 'vision':
  bidirectional_mask = tokens == _token_utils.SOFT_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER
  sliding_attention_mask = (
      _attention_mask.make_causal_bidirectional_attention_mask(
          inputs_mask,
          bidirectional_mask=bidirectional_mask,
      )
  )
```

Source: `gemma/gm/nn/gemma4/_transformer.py` in [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main).

Then the model uses that separate mask only for local sliding blocks:

```python
attn_mask = inputs.attention_mask
if (
    inputs.sliding_attention_mask is not None
    and block.attn_type == _modules.AttentionType.LOCAL_SLIDING
):
  attn_mask = inputs.sliding_attention_mask
```

Source: `gemma/gm/nn/gemma4/_transformer.py` in [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main).

Finally, local sliding attention intersects the selected attention mask with the sliding window:

```python
if self.attn_type == AttentionType.LOCAL_SLIDING:
  if self.sliding_window_size is None:
    raise ValueError(
        'Sliding_window_size must be set if Local Sliding attention type'
    )
  sliding_mask = _create_sliding_mask(
      segment_pos,
      cache_positions=cache_positions,
      sliding_window_size=self.sliding_window_size,
  )
  # [batch_size, seq_len, cache_size]
  attn_mask *= sliding_mask
```

Source: `gemma/gm/nn/gemma4/_modules.py` in [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main).

So this reference implementation seems to implement:

```text
global/full: causal
local_sliding: (causal OR vision_bidirectional) AND sliding_window
```

## Reference implementation: vLLM

I also checked [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), locally at commit `88d34c6409` on `releases/v0.20.0`.

vLLM appears to encode the same full-vs-sliding distinction explicitly. It precomputes non-sliding/full layer indices when `use_bidirectional_attention == "vision"`:

```python
# --- Precompute full-attention layer indices for bidi clearing ---
self._full_attn_layer_idxs: frozenset[int] = frozenset()
text_config = config.text_config
if getattr(text_config, "use_bidirectional_attention", None) == "vision":
    layer_types = getattr(text_config, "layer_types", None)
    if layer_types:
        self._full_attn_layer_idxs = frozenset(
            i for i, lt in enumerate(layer_types) if lt != "sliding_attention"
        )
```

Source: `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` in [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm).

Before running decoder layers, vLLM clears the multimodal prefix range for full-attention layers:

```python
# Gemma4 bidi: clear mm_prefix_range for full_attention layers.
# Must run here (outside @support_torch_compile boundary) because
# _run_decoder_layers is inside a compiled graph where Python
# side effects are eliminated.
self._clear_mm_prefix_for_full_attn_layers()
```

And the helper documents the intended behavior:

```python
def _clear_mm_prefix_for_full_attn_layers(self) -> None:
    """Clear mm_prefix_range for non-sliding layers.

    Gemma4 with use_bidirectional_attention='vision' applies
    bidirectional attention only to sliding_attention layers.
    Full attention layers use plain causal masking.

    Uses _full_attn_layer_idxs (precomputed in __init__) for O(1)
    lookup instead of per-call regex parsing.
    """
```

Source: `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` in [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm).

vLLM also filters oversized image ranges before installing the multimodal prefix/bidirectional range:

```python
# Gemma4 bidi: skip ranges that exceed the sliding
# window. When image tokens > sliding_window, bidi causes
# early image tokens to attend to the entire image
# (e.g. 6 → 1092 targets), degrading spatial precision.
# Per-range filtering keeps bidi for small images/video
# frames while skipping oversized images.
hf_text_config = self.model_config.hf_text_config
_bidi_sw = getattr(hf_text_config, "sliding_window", None)

for req_id in self.input_batch.req_ids:
    image_doc_ranges = []
    req_state = self.requests[req_id]
    for mm_feature in req_state.mm_features:
        pos_info = mm_feature.mm_position
        img_doc_range = pos_info.extract_embeds_range()
        for r in img_doc_range:
            if _bidi_sw is not None and (r[1] - r[0] + 1) > _bidi_sw:
                continue
            image_doc_ranges.append(r)
```

Source: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` in [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm).

This makes vLLM behavior closer to:

```text
full_attention:
  causal

sliding_attention:
  (causal AND sliding_window) OR vision_bidirectional,
  but only for image ranges whose length is <= sliding_window
```

## Minimal example

Assume:

```text
sliding_window = 1024
image tokens = positions 0..1099
```

For an image query token at position `0` and image key token at position `1099`:

- In Transformers `sliding_attention`, they are visible to each other because they are in the same `block_sequence_ids` group.
- In official `google/gemma`, they should not be visible in a local sliding layer because the final mask is intersected with the sliding window.
- In vLLM, this image range has length `1100 > 1024`, so the multimodal bidirectional range is skipped and the pair is not visible through vision-bidi.

For full/global layers:

- In Transformers, image tokens inside the same block are also bidirectionally visible.
- In official `google/gemma`, full/global layers appear to remain causal.
- In vLLM, full attention layers explicitly clear `mm_prefix_range` and remain causal.

For normal output text tokens, I believe all implementations still obey the causal sliding window in local sliding layers. The question here is specifically about the image-token blockwise bidirectional overlay and whether it should apply to full layers or bypass the sliding-window boundary.

## Expected behavior / question

Could you confirm the intended Gemma4 behavior for `use_bidirectional_attention="vision"`?

Should Transformers match the official `google/gemma` behavior:

```text
full_attention:
  causal

sliding_attention:
  (causal OR vision_blockwise_overlay) AND sliding_window
```

or is the current Transformers behavior intentional?

## Environment

- Transformers version: current `main` branch
- Models: Gemma4 / Gemma4Unified
- Reference implementations checked:
  - [`google-deepmind/gemma`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/gemma/tree/main), local commit `ab5a660`
  - [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), local commit `88d34c6409`

title: Several models hardcode `torch.float64` in their forward pass, crashing on MPS (Apple Silicon)
body:
### Summary

While auditing recent models for Apple Silicon (MPS) compatibility, I found two models that crash during a normal forward pass on MPS because they hardcode `torch.float64`, which the MPS backend does not support (`TypeError: Cannot convert a MPS Tensor to float64 dtype as the MPS framework doesn't support float64`). 

These are distinct from the `build_2d_sinusoidal_position_embedding` family already tracked in #46159.

### Affected code

1. **MusicFlamingo**, `apply_rotary_time_emb` ([modular_musicflamingo.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/musicflamingo/modular_musicflamingo.py)): upcasts hidden states to `float64` inside the rotary time embedding, which runs on every forward, so any MusicFlamingo inference on MPS crashes. The result is cast back to the original dtype immediately afterwards, so the `float64` intermediate adds no precision for `float32`/`bfloat16` and only breaks MPS.
2. **UDOP**, `combine_image_text_embeddings` ([modeling_udop.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/udop/modeling_udop.py)): casts `bbox` to `float64`. The value is only compared against `0.0` and `1.0`, so `float64` is not needed.

### Reproduction (MPS, e.g. Apple Silicon)

```python
import torch
from transformers.models.musicflamingo.modeling_musicflamingo import apply_rotary_time_emb

x = torch.randn(1, 2, 4, 8, device="mps")
apply_rotary_time_emb(x, torch.randn_like(x), torch.randn_like(x))
# TypeError: Cannot convert a MPS Tensor to float64 dtype ...
```

```python
import torch
from transformers.models.udop.modeling_udop import combine_image_text_embeddings

combine_image_text_embeddings(
    torch.randn(1, 196, 8, device="mps"), torch.randn(1, 5, 8, device="mps"),
    torch.rand(1, 5, 4, device="mps"), None, torch.ones(1, 5, device="mps"), num_patches=14,
)
# TypeError: Cannot convert a MPS Tensor to float64 dtype ...
```

Both run fine on CPU and CUDA (which support `float64`); the failure is MPS-specific.

### Proposed fix

Fall back to `float32` on MPS and keep `float64` elsewhere, matching the existing precedent in `generation_whisper.py` (`torch.float32 if device.type == "mps" else torch.float64`). This leaves CPU and CUDA behavior unchanged and makes both forward passes run on MPS. I have this implemented with MPS regression tests and can open a PR.

### Audit context

I checked roughly 50 recent models on MPS (text, vision, audio, OCR, multimodal). Hardcoded `float64` is the only MPS crash class I found; the rest run correctly. The sinusoidal-position-embedding instances are already covered by #46159, so this issue is only about the two remaining, unrelated sites above.

### Environment

- transformers: main
- torch: 2.11.0
- platform: macOS, Apple Silicon (MPS)

title: AutoProcessor reports “Unrecognized image processor” when required vision backend is missing
body:
### System Info

Observed with `transformers==5.12.1` in an environment with `torch` installed but `torchvision` missing.

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [x] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

```python
  from transformers import AutoProcessor

  AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct")
```

In an environment where torchvision is **not** installed, this can fail with:
```
ValueError: Unrecognized image processor in HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct...
```
This is misleading because the model/config can be recognized; the real issue is that the image processor implementation is unavailable due to a missing optional dependency. Installing `torchvision` makes the same processor load successfully.

This does not affect every vision processor equally. Some models can fall back to a PIL-based image processor when `torchvision` is unavailable and Pillow is installed. The issue is specifically that when no usable mapped backend implementation can be imported, the auto processor path should surface a dependency/backend error instead of an “unrecognized image processor” error.

### Expected behavior

The error should explain that no mapped image processor backend class could be loaded and suggest installing the missing backend dependency, rather than implying that the image processor or model type is unrecognized.

title: Aria: get_number_of_image_patches returns wrong count with max_image_size=980 when best resolution has odd 490 multiples
body:
## System Info

```
transformers version: main (latest)
Python: 3.10
torch: 2.6
```

## Who can help?

@zucchini-nlp @yonigozlan (Aria model maintainers)

## Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

## Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder
- [x] My own task or dataset (multi-modal / vision)

## Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AriaProcessor

processor = AriaProcessor.from_pretrained("rhymes-ai/Aria")

# max_image_size=980 is the default; split_image=True triggers the bug
images_kwargs = {"max_image_size": 980, "split_image": True}

# Image size where select_best_resolution picks [490, 980]
# (a portrait image, best matched to the (1,2) grid slot = [490, 980])
height, width = 300, 600  # aspect ratio ~1:2

num_patches = processor.image_processor.get_number_of_image_patches(
    height, width, images_kwargs
)
print(f"Reported num_patches: {num_patches}")  # prints 0 — WRONG, should be 1

# Confirm what divide_to_patches actually produces:
import torch
from transformers.image_transforms import divide_to_patches

dummy = torch.zeros(3, 490, 980)  # the padded image at best_resolution
actual_patches = divide_to_patches(dummy, patch_size=980)
print(f"Actual patches: {len(actual_patches)}")  # prints 1
```

Similarly for resolution `[980, 490]` (landscape image matching the (2,1) grid):

```python
# resized_height=980, resized_width=490, max_image_size=980
# 980 // 980 * 490 // 980 = 1 * 0 = 0   ← wrong, should be 1
```

And for resolution `[980, 1470]` (2×3 grid):

```python
# resized_height=980, resized_width=1470, max_image_size=980
# 980 // 980 * 1470 // 980 = 1 * 1 = 1  ← wrong, should be 1*2=2
```

## Expected behavior

`get_number_of_image_patches` should return the same count as the number of patches `get_image_patches` actually produces. Internally, `get_image_patches` calls `divide_to_patches(padded_image, patch_size=max_image_size)`, which iterates `range(0, height, patch_size)` — equivalent to `ceil(height / patch_size)` patches per dimension.

Expected formula:

```python
import math
num_patches = math.ceil(resized_height / max_image_size) * math.ceil(resized_width / max_image_size)
```

## Actual behavior

The current code uses integer floor division:

```python
num_patches = 1 if not split_image else resized_height // max_image_size * resized_width // max_image_size
```

`//` truncates toward zero, so when `resized_height < max_image_size` (e.g., `490 // 980 = 0`) the result is wrong. More broadly, any time `resized_height` or `resized_width` is not an exact multiple of `max_image_size`, the count is too low.

With the default `max_image_size=980`, the `split_resolutions` are `el[0]*490, el[1]*490` for small integers `el`. Any resolution with an **odd** `el` value (1, 3, 5, 7) produces a dimension that is not a multiple of 980:

| Best resolution | Floor result | Correct (ceil) |
|-----------------|-------------|-----------------|
| [490, 980]      | 0           | 1               |
| [980, 490]      | 0           | 1               |
| [490, 1470]     | 0           | 2               |
| [1470, 490]     | 0           | 2               |
| [980, 1470]     | 1           | 2               |
| [1470, 980]     | 1           | 2               |
| [1470, 1470]    | 1           | 4               |

When `num_patches` is wrong, `get_multimodal_data` computes the wrong `num_image_tokens`, causing visual embeddings to be misaligned with text token positions.

## Affected files

The same bug appears in three places (the latter two are auto-generated from the first):

- `src/transformers/models/aria/modular_aria.py` (line 514) ← fix here
- `src/transformers/models/aria/image_processing_aria.py` (line 222) ← auto-generated
- `src/transformers/models/aria/image_processing_pil_aria.py` (line 226) ← auto-generated
author: arnavkewalram

title: LabelSmoother ignores num_items_in_batch, inflating gradients by ~gradient_accumulation_steps with label smoothing
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` 5.13.0.dev0 (main, 9fd7b6789d; also reproduced on 36193bf)
- `torch` 2.11.0, Python 3.13.5, macOS 15.6 arm64 (forced CPU via `use_cpu=True`; not device-specific — also reproduces on the default MPS device)

### Who can help?

@muellerzr @SunMarc

### Reproduction

```python
import torch, datasets
from transformers import (AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer,
                          TrainingArguments, DataCollatorForLanguageModeling, TrainerCallback)

name = "trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2ForCausalLM-2.5"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name); tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
ds = datasets.load_dataset("Salesforce/wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1", split="train[:200]")
ds = ds.filter(lambda e: len(e["text"].strip()) > 0)
ds = ds.map(lambda e: tok(e["text"], max_length=16, padding="max_length", truncation=True), batched=True)
coll = DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(tokenizer=tok, mlm=False)

def run(bs, gas):
    out = []
    class CB(TrainerCallback):
        def on_log(self, a, s, c, logs=None, **k):
            if logs and "grad_norm" in logs: out.append(logs["grad_norm"])
    m = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(name, dtype=torch.float32)
    args = TrainingArguments("/tmp/.ls_repro", per_device_train_batch_size=bs,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=gas, label_smoothing_factor=0.1, max_steps=3,
        logging_steps=1, learning_rate=1e-4, max_grad_norm=0.0, report_to=[], use_cpu=True)
    Trainer(m, args, train_dataset=ds, data_collator=coll, callbacks=[CB()]).train()
    return out

base = run(8, 1)   # effective batch 8, no accumulation
gas  = run(1, 8)   # same effective batch 8, via 8 accumulation steps
print("base (bs=8, gas=1):", [round(x, 4) for x in base])
print("gas  (bs=1, gas=8):", [round(x, 4) for x in gas])
print("ratio gas/base    :", [round(g / b, 2) for b, g in zip(base, gas) if b])
```

Output on current main:

```
base (bs=8, gas=1): [0.3281, 0.3209, 0.3021]
gas  (bs=1, gas=8): [2.9545, 3.0083, 2.6038]
ratio gas/base    : [9.01, 9.37, 8.62]
```

Both runs have the same effective batch (8), so the grad norms should match. With `label_smoothing_factor=0.1` the accumulation run is ~`gradient_accumulation_steps`× larger. Set `label_smoothing_factor=0.0` and the ratio is ~1.0.

### Expected behavior

Grad norms and logged loss should be independent of how the effective batch is split into accumulation steps — as they already are without label smoothing.

### Root cause

With label smoothing the loss comes from `LabelSmoother`, not the model:

- `_get_num_items_in_batch` returns a non-`None` count because `model_accepts_loss_kwargs` is True, so `training_step` skips the `1 / gradient_accumulation_steps` normalization (the `if (not self.model_accepts_loss_kwargs or num_items_in_batch is None) and self.compute_loss_func is None:` guard).
- But `compute_loss` calls `self.label_smoother(outputs, labels, ...)` without `num_items_in_batch`, and `LabelSmoother.__call__` mean-reduces over the current micro-batch's active tokens (`trainer_pt_utils.py`).
- So neither path normalizes by the effective batch: the accumulated gradient becomes `sum_i(S_i / N_i)` instead of `sum_i(S_i) / sum_i(N_i)`.

The grad-accum change that added `num_items_in_batch` (#34198) only touched `trainer.py`, not `trainer_pt_utils.py`, so `LabelSmoother` was never wired up. The same `num_items_in_batch` is already passed into the `compute_loss_func` branch right next to it.

### Fix

Passing `num_items_in_batch` into `LabelSmoother` and using it as the denominator (falling back to the active-token count when `None`) restores the ratio:

```
gas (bs=1, gas=8): [0.3281, 0.3209, 0.3021]   # ratio 1.0
```

This shifts the loss/grad magnitude by ~`gradient_accumulation_steps` for existing label-smoothing + accumulation runs (the old values were over-scaled). Single-device and default DDP token averaging become exact; legacy DataParallel keeps the same `n_gpu` approximation the `compute_loss_func` path already has.

I have the fix and a red→green regression test ready — happy to open a PR.
author: Incheonkirin

title: LoRA fine-tuning of an FP8 checkpoint is blocked: `get_peft_model` does not clear `validate_quantization_for_training` (QuantizationMethod.FP8)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` 5.9.0
- `peft` 0.19.1
- `accelerate` 1.13.0
- `torch` 2.9.1 (CUDA 12.9)
- Python 3.12
- Platform: SageMaker training job, 2× p5.48xlarge (16× H100 80GB), FSDP `full_shard`, `attn_implementation="eager"`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (284B MoE, published **FP8-only** — `quantization_config.quant_method == "fp8"`, e4m3, 128×128 weight blocks)

### Who can help?

@SunMarc @MekkCyber (quantization), @BenjaminBossan (PEFT)

### Description

Fine-tuning an FP8-quantized checkpoint with LoRA fails at `Trainer.__init__`:

```
ValueError: The model you are trying to fine-tune is quantized with QuantizationMethod.FP8
but that quantization method do not support training. Please open an issue on GitHub ...
```

The error message and the docs both say the supported route for a quantized base model is to **attach trainable LoRA adapters** on top. We do exactly that via `peft.get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(...))` **before** constructing the `Trainer`, yet the guard still raises.

Root cause (transformers 5.9.0, `trainer_utils.py::validate_quantization_for_training`):

```python
_is_quantized_and_base_model = getattr(model, "is_quantized", False) and not getattr(
    model, "_hf_peft_config_loaded", False
)
...
elif _is_quantized_and_base_model and not _quantization_method_supports_training:
    raise ValueError(... "do not support training" ...)
```

- `get_peft_model` wraps the model in a `PeftModel`, but **does not set `_hf_peft_config_loaded` on the (inner) base model** (confirmed: that attribute is never assigned anywhere in `peft`; it is only set by transformers' native `PeftAdapterMixin.add_adapter`/`load_adapter`, `integrations/peft.py`).
- `PeftModel.__getattr__` proxies `is_quantized` to the FP8 base → `True`.
- So `_is_quantized_and_base_model` stays `True`, and because the FP8 quantizer reports `is_trainable == False`, the **`elif` branch raises** — even though a LoRA adapter is attached.

Note the earlier `if` branch *does* exempt PEFT models (`... and not _is_peft_model(model) ...`), but the `elif` (quant-method-not-trainable) has **no `_is_peft_model` / `_hf_peft_config_loaded` exemption** when the wrapper came from `get_peft_model`. As a result there is **no documented way** to LoRA-fine-tune an FP8 base via the standard `get_peft_model` flow.

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from datasets import Dataset

model_id = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"   # any FP8 checkpoint, e.g. an FP8 DeepSeek-V3.1
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_id, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="eager", trust_remote_code=True
)
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)

# Attach LoRA exactly as the error message / docs recommend
model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, task_type="CAUSAL_LM"))

ds = Dataset.from_dict({"text": ["hello world"]}).map(lambda x: tok(x["text"]), remove_columns=["text"])
Trainer(model=model, args=TrainingArguments(output_dir="/tmp/x"), train_dataset=ds)
# -> ValueError: ... QuantizationMethod.FP8 ... do not support training
```

### Expected behavior

One of the following:

1. A `get_peft_model`-wrapped model (`_is_peft_model(model) is True`) should **bypass the `elif` "quant-method-not-trainable" branch**, since the frozen FP8 base is never updated — only the bf16 LoRA adapters are. (The first `if` branch already exempts PEFT models; the `elif` arguably should too.)
2. Or: clear, official documentation that FP8 checkpoints cannot be LoRA-fine-tuned at all, and that `model.add_adapter(...)` (which sets `_hf_peft_config_loaded`) is/ isn't a supported substitute — including whether autograd actually backpropagates through FP8 block-quantized linears to the adapters.

### Open questions for maintainers

- Is `model.add_adapter(lora_config)` (native API, sets `_hf_peft_config_loaded=True`) the intended supported path for LoRA-on-FP8, or does it merely bypass the guard while the backward pass through FP8 linears is still unsupported?
- Does this overlap with #46295 (Training Support for FP8) and the closed-without-resolution #41516 / #37927? If FP8 LoRA is intended to work, the `get_peft_model` flow appears to be the blocker.

### Related issues

- #46295 (open) — Training Support for FP8
- #41516 (closed, no resolution) — DeepSeek V3.1 LoRA → same FP8 ValueError
- #37927 (closed) — request FP8 training support
- #39410 (open) — FP8 training for MP/TP

title: GlmMoeDsa: head_dim→qk_rope_head_dim attribute_map silently clobbers the rope head dim (GLM-5.2)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` 5.8.1
- Model: GLM-5.2 (`model_type: glm_moe_dsa`, `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`)

### Description

`GlmMoeDsaConfig` declares `attribute_map = {"head_dim": "qk_rope_head_dim"}`, so `head_dim` is an
alias for `qk_rope_head_dim`. But GLM-5.2's released `config.json` sets **both** fields with
**different** values (`"head_dim": 192`, `"qk_rope_head_dim": 64`). Because of the alias, `head_dim`
(192, which equals `qk_nope_head_dim`) silently **overwrites** the real `qk_rope_head_dim` (64).

### Reproduction

```python
from transformers.models.glm_moe_dsa.configuration_glm_moe_dsa import GlmMoeDsaConfig

c = GlmMoeDsaConfig(head_dim=192, qk_rope_head_dim=64, qk_nope_head_dim=192, kv_lora_rank=512)
print(c.qk_rope_head_dim)   # -> 192   (expected 64)
print(GlmMoeDsaConfig.attribute_map)
# {'num_local_experts': 'n_routed_experts', 'head_dim': 'qk_rope_head_dim'}
```

Loading the released GLM-5.2 `config.json` (which contains both keys) reproduces the same:
`config.qk_rope_head_dim == 192`.

### Why this is a bug

The checkpoint geometry pins `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, not 192:
- `kv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight` is `[576, 6144]` → `576 = kv_lora_rank(512) + qk_rope_head_dim(64)`.
- `q_b_proj.weight` is `[16384, 6144→]` → `16384 / 64 heads = 256 = qk_nope_head_dim(192) + qk_rope_head_dim(64)`.

With `qk_rope_head_dim` clobbered to 192, the MLA head is computed as `512 + 192 = 704` instead of
`512 + 64 = 576`, which breaks MLA weight loading in downstream runtimes (e.g. vLLM raises a
`narrow(... 704) exceeds dimension size (576)` during `fused_qkv_a_proj` load). `head_dim` is also
ambiguous for an MLA attention head whose q/k/v sub-dims differ, so aliasing it onto the rope dim
is surprising.

### Suggested fix

Drop the `"head_dim": "qk_rope_head_dim"` entry from `GlmMoeDsaConfig.attribute_map` (and/or remove
the redundant `head_dim` from the released `config.json` so the explicit `qk_rope_head_dim` stands).
Happy to open a PR if that's the preferred direction.

### Expected behavior

`config.qk_rope_head_dim` should be 64 (its explicit value and the checkpoint-true rope dim), not be
overwritten by `head_dim`.

title: FR: Implement Downstream Integration Smoke Tests in CI/CD to Prevent Ecosystem Regression
body:
### Feature request


​We request the addition of Downstream Integration Smoke Tests within the transformers CI/CD automation pipeline (GitHub Actions/CircleCI). Before a new release is cut, the test matrix should pull down and execute basic smoke generation scripts against a select group of foundational, high-impact downstream structural decoding packages (e.g., outlines, transformers_cfg, lmformatenforcer).
​Additionally, if a private or internal API handling token/byte structures must be removed or moved to a compiled backend, we request a formalized deprecation warning cycle alongside a stable, public utility endpoint to retrieve bidirectional token-to-byte maps.

### Motivation


Whenever a minor or patch version refactors internal layout paths, the upstream test suite passes completely green because it only evaluates native tasks. However, the wider ecosystem immediately breaks.
Recent internal shifts—such as moving PreTrainedTokenizerBase out of tokenization_utils or completely wiping python-level attributes like bytes_to_unicode, .byte_encoder, and .byte_decoder—instantly broke multiple context-free grammar parsers and guided decoding engines.
While these are technically internal namespaces, deep engineering tools must hook into token-to-byte maps to build logit filtering matrices. Deleting or relocating them without a stable public alternative or a deprecation warning forces end-users into version lock or requires maintaining fragile runtime monkey patches to keep enterprise applications functional on newer releases.

### Your contribution

To prevent production applications from experiencing immediate ImportError or AttributeError failures on the latest versions while a permanent architectural solution is developed, the community is forced to rely on the following runtime patch. This can be integrated or used as a reference for the missing backward-compatible hooks:


```python
import sys
import transformers

# 1. Bridge lmformatenforcer path changes
if not hasattr(transformers.tokenization_utils, 'PreTrainedTokenizerBase'):
    import transformers.tokenization_utils_base
    transformers.tokenization_utils.PreTrainedTokenizerBase = transformers.tokenization_utils_base.PreTrainedTokenizerBase

# 2. Bridge transformers_cfg logging namespace relocations
if not hasattr(transformers, 'logging'):
    import transformers.utils.logging
    transformers.logging = transformers.utils.logging

# 3. Independent reconstruction of the removed GPT2 byte-mapping attributes
def get_clean_byte_maps():
    bs = list(range(ord("!"), ord("~") + 1)) + list(range(ord("¡"), ord("¬") + 1)) + list(range(ord("®"), ord("ÿ") + 1))
    cs = bs[:]
    n = 0
    for b in range(256):
        if b not in bs:
            bs.append(b)
            cs.append(256 + n)
            n += 1
    encoder = dict(zip(bs, [chr(x) for x in cs]))
    decoder = {v: k for k, v in encoder.items()}
    return encoder, decoder

byte_encoder_map, byte_decoder_map = get_clean_byte_maps()

# Inject attributes back onto the target base classes for downstream compatibility
for cls_name in ['GPT2Tokenizer', 'GPT2TokenizerFast']:
    if hasattr(transformers, cls_name):
        cls = getattr(transformers, cls_name)
        cls.byte_encoder = byte_encoder_map
        cls.byte_decoder = byte_decoder_map
```

  block_scores = scores.amax(dim=-1).amax(dim=1)

title: Is transformers 5.12.1 requires tokenizers<=0.23.0,>=0.22.0 really right?
body:
https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/releases/tag/v0.23.1 says that:

tokenizers 0.23.1 is the first proper stable release in the 0.23 line — 0.23.0 only ever shipped as rc0 because the release pipeline itself was broken (Node side hadn't shipped multi-platform binaries since 2023, Python side was on pyo3 0.27 without free-threaded support). 0.23.1 is the version where everything actually goes out the door together: full Node multi-platform wheels for the first time in years, Python 3.14 (regular and free-threaded 3.14t), full type hints for every Python class, and a stack of measurable perf wins on the BPE / added-vocab hot paths.

There is no functional 0.23.0 published — we tag 0.23.1 directly so users don't accidentally pull a never-shipped version.

So we should have an upper bound of <0.23 or <0.24?

title: ZeRO-3 zero.Init does not partition composite minimax_m3_vl language submodule -> OOM on multi-GPU load
body:
**Env:** transformers 5.12.1, deepspeed 0.18.9, torch 2.12.0+cu130, peft 0.19.1, bitsandbytes 0.49.2, accelerate 1.14.0; 8x B200 (178GB) / 2TB RAM; model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 (428B sparse MoE VL, minimax_m3_vl).

Loading `AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", torch_dtype=bf16)` under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 — with `HfDeepSpeedConfig(ds_cfg)` held alive and `is_deepspeed_zero3_enabled()` True before the call — OOMs on load. The composite `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration` builds `language_model` (the 428B sparse MoE) as a nested submodule whose parameters do not appear to be created inside the active `zero.Init` context, so they materialize full-size rather than partitioned (~1/8).

**Workaround that works:** export a text-only checkpoint (keep `language_model.*`, strip the prefix -> `model.*`/`lm_head.*`, drop the vision tower) and load the standalone `MiniMaxM3VLForCausalLM` — that partitions correctly under `zero.Init`.

**Ask:** composite VLM `from_pretrained` should propagate the `zero.Init` context to all nested submodules, or document the text-only LM load path for fine-tuning the LM under ZeRO-3.

RTDetrForObjectDetection raises a TypeError when num_feature_levels is set higher than the number of backbone output levels (default being 3). Normal inference with default config is unaffected. The bug is latent until num_feature_levels is explicitly increased, for example when experimenting with additional decoder feature levels for small object detection.

Root cause: in RTDetrModel.forward, when num_feature_levels > len(sources), the first extra level is built with a misplaced [-1] index:

```python
# Line 1626 in modeling_rt_detr.py (generated from modular_rt_detr.py line 1865)
# BUGGY: passes the full list to conv2d, then tries to index [-1] on the result
sources.append(self.decoder_input_proj[_len_sources](encoder_outputs.last_hidden_state)[-1])

# The correct pattern already exists on the very next iteration (line 1627):
sources.append(self.decoder_input_proj[i](encoder_outputs.last_hidden_state[-1]))
```

encoder_outputs.last_hidden_state is a list of feature-map tensors. The [-1] index should select the last tensor from the list before passing it to the Conv2d projection layer, not after. The correct pattern is already used on the immediately following line, making the fix a single bracket move.

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`Qwen3_5TextConfig.base_model_tp_plan` only covers `self_attn.*` and `mlp.*` layers:

```python
base_model_tp_plan = {
    "layers.*.self_attn.q_proj": "colwise",
    "layers.*.self_attn.k_proj": "colwise",
    "layers.*.self_attn.v_proj": "colwise",
    "layers.*.self_attn.o_proj": "rowwise",
    "layers.*.self_attn.q_norm": "replicated_with_grad_allreduce",
    "layers.*.self_attn.k_norm": "replicated_with_grad_allreduce",
    "layers.*.mlp.gate_proj": "colwise",
    "layers.*.mlp.up_proj": "colwise",
    "layers.*.mlp.down_proj": "rowwise",
}
```

Qwen3.5 is a hybrid model: roughly 75% of its decoder layers are `linear_attention` layers backed by `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet` (Gated Delta Net / GDA). These layers have their own projection matrices (`in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `in_proj_b`, `in_proj_a`, `out_proj`) that are absent from `base_model_tp_plan`. This produces two failures at TP>1:
**Failure 1: OOM when loading the model at TP>1**

The `linear_attn` weights are not sharded, so each rank holds a full copy. For `Qwen3.5-9B` at TP=4 this causes an out-of-memory error before any inference starts.

**Failure 2: RuntimeError during `model.generate()`**

Adding the `linear_attn` projections with the same `"colwise"` / `"rowwise"` pattern as `self_attn` does not fix this. `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet.forward` passes `in_proj_qkv`'s output directly through a depthwise `Conv1d` (with `groups=conv_dim`, where `conv_dim = key_dim*2 + value_dim = 8192`). With plain `"colwise"` TP, each rank receives only `conv_dim/TP = 2048` channels, but the `Conv1d` weight expects `8192`. A `torch.split([key_dim, key_dim, value_dim])` immediately after the conv has the same requirement.

```
RuntimeError: convolution(): expected the second dimension of the weight tensor
of shape [8192, 1, 4] to be 0 (2048 in channels divided by 8192 groups), got 1
```

### Root cause

`base_model_tp_plan` in `Qwen3_5TextConfig` is incomplete: it has no entries for any `linear_attn.*` submodule. Because roughly 75% of the model's layers use `linear_attention`, a large fraction of the parameters are not sharded at all when `tp_plan="auto"` is requested.

### Proposed fix

**File to edit: `src/transformers/models/qwen3_5/modular_qwen3_5.py`** (`configuration_qwen3_5.py` is auto-generated from it. The header says "Do NOT edit this file manually"; CI regenerates it from the modular source.)

Add `"colwise_gather_output"` entries for all `linear_attn` projections. `"colwise_gather_output"` is `ColwiseParallel(gather_output=True)`: the weight matrix is sharded across ranks (fixing the OOM), and the output activation is all-gathered before the next operation, so the forward pass sees the full tensor.

```python
base_model_tp_plan = {
    # ... existing self_attn and mlp entries unchanged ...
    "layers.*.linear_attn.in_proj_qkv": "colwise_gather_output",
    "layers.*.linear_attn.in_proj_z":   "colwise_gather_output",
    "layers.*.linear_attn.in_proj_b":   "colwise_gather_output",
    "layers.*.linear_attn.in_proj_a":   "colwise_gather_output",
    "layers.*.linear_attn.out_proj":    "colwise_gather_output",
}
```

`conv1d` is a `nn.Conv1d`, not a `nn.Linear`, so it does not appear in the TP plan. With `colwise_gather_output` on `in_proj_qkv`, the activations are gathered before `conv1d` runs, so the conv layer needs no TP plan entry.

### Why not `"colwise"` / `"rowwise"` (the self_attn pattern)?

The `self_attn` pattern works because `q/k/v_proj` outputs feed into independent per-head computations that decompose naturally across ranks, and `o_proj` with `"rowwise"` expects a sharded input from the preceding colwise-sharded value projection. The GDA forward pass does not have this property. `in_proj_qkv`'s output is a single concatenated `[Q, K, V]` tensor fed directly into a depthwise conv and then split. Neither operation is rank-decomposable. `"colwise_gather_output"` handles this by sharding the weights and inserting an all-gather before those ops.


### Expected behavior

I would expect the model instantiation and generate to work.

title: Qwen3.5 Does not work with variable length inputs using position_ids
body:
### System Info

The current implementation of Qwen3.5 linear attention assumes that user passes cu_seqlen arguments explicitly as opposed to just position_ids like older models. While the problem can be circumvented by passing these inputs, it becomes a problem in downstream packages (such as Verl) that assume the same interface between HuggingFace based language models. The problem is also silent and does not raise any errors but simply performs incorrect computation when cu_seqlen(s) are omitted with variable length inputs.

To fix this, the variable sequence length inputs should be treated the same way in Qwen3.5 as all other models. Also, the current torch fallback silently fails even when the cu_seqlen inputs are passed as it never uses them.

title: _prefill: cache.get_seq_length() returns device tensor, breaks slice arithmetic for static cache + torch.compile on non-CUDA backends
body:
### System Info

  - transformers version: 5.5.3
  - PyTorch version: 2.10.0
  - Python version: 3.10.12
  - OS: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
  - Device: CPU (using `torch.compile(backend="inductor")`)
  - Last working version: transformers 5.2.0
  - First broken version: transformers 5.5.3 (where _prefill was introduced)


### Who can help?

@ArthurZucker @gante 

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import torch

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
model.generation_config.cache_implementation = "static"
model.forward = torch.compile(model.forward, backend="inductor")

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
input_ids = tokenizer("Hello world", return_tensors="pt").input_ids

# First call: works
output1 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)
print("First call OK:", output1.shape)

# Second call: CRASHES
output2 = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1, do_sample=False)
print("Second call OK:", output2.shape)

**Note**: On CUDA this may not crash due to CUDA graph replay masking the bug. 
To reproduce on CUDA, you can add a `torch._dynamo.reset()` between calls to force retracing.

### Expected behavior

Multiple `model.generate()` calls with static cache and `torch.compile` should work
without crashing, regardless of the backend device.

## Root Cause Analysis

1. `cache_utils.py` line 383: `self.cumulative_length = torch.tensor([0], dtype=int)`
   - Comment says: "Very important that it's a tensor here, to avoid recompiling"
   
2. `cache_utils.py` line 461: `get_seq_length()` returns this tensor directly
   - Return type annotation says `-> int` but actual return is `torch.Tensor`

3. `generation/utils.py` `_prefill()`: Uses `past_length` in int arithmetic
   - `next_sequence_length = input_ids.shape[1] - past_length` → produces tensor

4. `generation/utils.py` line 502: `prepare_inputs_for_generation(next_sequence_length: int | None)`
   - Type contract violated: receives tensor instead of int

5. `generation/utils.py` line 532: `input_ids[:, -next_sequence_length:]`
   - Tensor-as-slice-index produces wrong (0-length) result

## Suggested Fix

In `_prefill()`, convert `past_length` to Python int after calling `get_seq_length()`:

```python
if (cache := model_kwargs.get("past_key_values")) is not None:
    past_length = cache.get_seq_length()
    if isinstance(past_length, torch.Tensor):
        past_length = int(past_length.item())
```

This is safe because:
- `cumulative_length` remains a tensor on the model (torch.compile compatibility preserved)
- Only the local variable in `_prefill` is converted
- On CUDA (where `get_seq_length()` may already return int): isinstance check is False → no-op
- Restores the `int | None` type contract for `next_sequence_length`

  This worked correctly in transformers 5.2.0 where _prefill() did not exist.
  The regression was introduced when _prefill was added (transformers >= 5.5.0)
  which introduced cache-aware token slicing using cache.get_seq_length().

  In 5.2.0: generate() always passed full input_ids to model.forward (no slicing).
  In 5.5.3: _prefill slices input_ids based on cache.get_seq_length(), but doesn't
  handle the case where get_seq_length() returns a tensor instead of int.

title: CohereASR training-loss double-shift bug (same pattern as Moonshine #46784)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.13.0.dev0 (main branch at commit dc5a497c18)
- - Platform: Windows
- - - Python version: 3.x
- - - - Using GPU: N/A (code-level bug, not runtime)

### Who can help?

@eustlb @ebezzam @vasqu

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

aIn `src/transformers/models/cohere_asr/modular_cohere_asr.py`, `CohereAsrForConditionalGeneration.forward()` has a double-shift bug:

1. Labels are shifted right via `shift_tokens_right()` (line 483) to create `decoder_input_ids`
2. 2. Then `self.loss_function()` is called (line 503), which maps to `ForCausalLMLoss`
3. 3. `ForCausalLMLoss` shifts labels again internally (`labels[..., 1:]` in `loss/loss_utils.py` line 63-64)
This means the model trains against `labels[..., 1:]` instead of `labels`.

This is the **exact same bug** that was fixed in Moonshine in PR #46784 (commit d8c235494e). The Moonshine fix replaced `self.loss_function()` with `CrossEntropyLoss()`, but `CohereAsr` — which inherits from Moonshine and overrides `forward` — was not updated.

```python
# Buggy code (line 503 in modular_cohere_asr.py):
loss = self.loss_function(logits=logits, labels=labels, vocab_size=self.config.vocab_size)

# Should be:
loss_fct = CrossEntropyLoss()
loss = loss_fct(logits.reshape(-1, self.config.vocab_size), labels.reshape(-1))
```

### Expected behavior

Training loss should be computed directly against `labels` without any additional shifting, since `shift_tokens_right()` already handles the decoder input alignment. This matches the behavior of Whisper, Bart, and the now-fixed Moonshine model. The fix should use `CrossEntropyLoss()` instead of `self.loss_function()`, as done in Moonshine PR #46784.

title: [Gemma4] Audio (and vision) processing broken with 4‑bit quantization due to unsafe dtype cast in multimodal embedders
body:
### System Info


-   `transformers` version: 5.12.1
    
-   `bitsandbytes` version: 0.49.2
    
-   Platform: Linux, Python 3.13, CUDA 12.x
    
-   GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5090
    
-   Quantization config: `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4", bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16, bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True)`
    


### Who can help?


@ArthurZucker @zucchini-nlp


### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

```python

import torch
import librosa
from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor, BitsAndBytesConfig
MODEL_NAME = "google/gemma-4-12b-it"
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
 load_in_4bit=True,
 bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
 bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
 bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True
)
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(
 MODEL_NAME,
 quantization_config=bnb_config,
 device_map="cuda",
 dtype=torch.bfloat16
)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
# Simulate loading audio (replace with actual audio)
import numpy as np
audio_waveform = np.random.randn(16000 * 5).astype(np.float32)  # 5 seconds, float32 as returned by librosa
messages = [{
 "role": "user",
 "content": [
 {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this audio."},
 {"type": "audio", "audio": audio_waveform},
 ]
}]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
 messages,
 tokenize=True,
 return_dict=True,
 return_tensors="pt",
 add_generation_prompt=True,
).to(model.device)
# This will trigger the error
with torch.no_grad():
 model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=10)
```

### Expected behavior

The model should process the audio without dtype mismatch errors when loaded with 4‑bit quantization.


## Actual behavior

A `RuntimeError` is raised during the `masked_scatter` operation inside `Gemma4UnifiedModel.forward`:

```text

RuntimeError: masked_scatter_: expected self and source to have same dtypes but got BFloat16 and Byte
```
If the problematic cast inside the embedder is simply removed (see root cause), a different mismatch occurs:
```text

RuntimeError: masked_scatter_: expected self and source to have same dtypes but got BFloat16 and Float
```
## Full error trace (original)

```text

File .../modeling_gemma4_unified.py:1088, in Gemma4UnifiedModel.forward()
 inputs_embeds = inputs_embeds.masked_scatter(
 audio_mask.to(inputs_embeds.device), audio_features.to(inputs_embeds.device)
 )
RuntimeError: masked_scatter_: expected self and source to have same dtypes but got BFloat16 and Byte
```
## Root cause

The issue originates in `Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder.forward()` (used for audio, and similarly in `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` for vision) [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c96378c4136f5882fee50d8ff8ee1e9588a17eb6/src/transformers/models/gemma4_unified/modular_gemma4_unified.py#L897):

```python

class Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder(nn.Module):
 ...
 def forward(self, inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   # Additional dtype casting
   inputs_embeds = inputs_embeds.to(self.embedding_projection.weight.dtype)
   embs_normed = self.embedding_pre_projection_norm(inputs_embeds)
   return self.embedding_projection(embs_normed)
```
When the model is **not quantized**, `weight.dtype` is `torch.bfloat16` (or `float32`), and the cast is harmless.  
When loaded in **4‑bit**, `self.embedding_projection` becomes a `Linear4bit` layer whose `.weight` is stored as `torch.uint8` (the packed low‑precision data). The cast `inputs_embeds.to(weight.dtype)`  **destroys** the tensor by converting it to `uint8`, causing downstream operations to fail with `BFloat16` vs `Byte`.

Additionally, the audio input tensor coming from the processor is `float32`. Previously this was inadvertently cast to `bfloat16` via the same `weight.dtype` mechanism (when unquantized). With the line removed, the tensor stays `float32`, leading to the second mismatch (`bfloat16` vs `float32`).

Thus, two problems exist:

1.  The cast to `weight.dtype` is unsafe when the model is quantized.
    
2.  The embedder does not ensure the input matches the model’s _compute_ dtype.
    

## Suggested fix

Replace the unsafe `weight.dtype` cast with a check for the layer’s actual compute dtype, which is available via `compute_dtype` attribute for `bitsandbytes` layers.

**[In](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c96378c4136f5882fee50d8ff8ee1e9588a17eb6/src/transformers/models/gemma4_unified/modular_gemma4_unified.py#L897) `Gemma4UnifiedMultimodalEmbedder.forward`:**

```python

def forward(self, inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
  if hasattr(self.embedding_projection, "compute_dtype"):
    target_dtype = self.embedding_projection.compute_dtype
  else:
    target_dtype = self.embedding_projection.weight.dtype
  inputs_embeds = inputs_embeds.to(target_dtype)
  embs_normed = self.embedding_pre_projection_norm(inputs_embeds)
  return self.embedding_projection(embs_normed)
```
**[In](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c96378c4136f5882fee50d8ff8ee1e9588a17eb6/src/transformers/models/gemma4_unified/modular_gemma4_unified.py#L866) `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder.forward`** (same pattern, for consistency and safety):

```python

def forward(self, pixel_values, image_position_ids):
 ...
  if hasattr(self.patch_dense, "compute_dtype"):
    target_dtype = self.patch_dense.compute_dtype
  else:
    target_dtype = self.patch_dense.weight.dtype
  hidden_states = self.patch_ln1(pixel_values.to(target_dtype))
  ...
```
This guarantees:

-   For normal `nn.Linear`: `target_dtype = weight.dtype` (exact previous behavior).
    
-   For `Linear4bit`: `target_dtype = compute_dtype` (e.g., `torch.bfloat16`), which matches the rest of the model and the expected input for the quantized layer.
    

It also eliminates the requirement for users to manually cast `input_features` before calling `generate()`.

## Additional context

-   The same bug affects **vision inputs** (images / videos) when quantized, though the trace might differ. The fix in `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` should be applied as well.
    
-   The issue is **not present** when quantization is disabled, which is why it has likely gone unnoticed.
    

Please apply the above changes to [`modular_gemma4_unified.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c96378c4136f5882fee50d8ff8ee1e9588a17eb6/src/transformers/models/gemma4_unified/modular_gemma4_unified.py#L897). Thank you!

title: PPFormulaNet training-loss double-shift: trains against labels[..., 1:] instead of labels
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.13.0.dev0 (main, commit `c96378c413`)
- Platform: macOS, Python 3.11 (code-level bug, no specific hardware required)

### Who can help?

@yonigozlan @zucchini-nlp (PPFormulaNet / Florence2 area)

### Description

`PPFormulaNetForConditionalGeneration.forward` builds `decoder_input_ids` by right-shifting the target with `shift_tokens_right` (`modular_pp_formulanet.py:386`), then computes the training loss with `self.loss_function` (which maps to `ForCausalLMLoss`). `ForCausalLMLoss` shifts the labels a **second** time (`labels[..., 1:]`, `loss/loss_utils.py:24-25`), so the model trains against `labels[..., 1:]` instead of `labels` — an off-by-one in the training loss.

This is the same class of bug that was fixed for Moonshine in #46784 (and is being fixed for CohereASR / Florence2). PPFormulaNet right-shifts `input_ids` rather than `labels`, but the effect is identical when `input_ids == labels` — the standard encoder-decoder training setup, and exactly what the model's own test inputs use (`input_ids` is set equal to the decoder target).

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import PPFormulaNetConfig, PPFormulaNetForConditionalGeneration

vision_config = {
    "image_size": 768, "patch_size": 16, "hidden_size": 48, "windows_size": 14,
    "num_hidden_layers": 1, "output_channels": 16, "num_attention_heads": 2,
    "global_attn_indexes": [1, 1, 1, 1], "mlp_dim": 1,
    "post_conv_in_channels": 16, "post_conv_mid_channels": 16,
    "post_conv_out_channels": 16, "decoder_hidden_size": 48,
}
text_config = {"decoder_ffn_dim": 16, "decoder_layers": 1, "d_model": 48, "vocab_size": 99}
config = PPFormulaNetConfig(text_config=text_config, vision_config=vision_config, num_hidden_layers=1)

model = PPFormulaNetForConditionalGeneration(config).eval()
V = config.text_config.vocab_size

torch.manual_seed(0)
target = torch.tensor([[5, 11, 23, 7, 42, 2]])     # input_ids == labels == decoder target
pixel_values = torch.rand(1, 3, 768, 768)

with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(pixel_values=pixel_values, input_ids=target, labels=target)

aligned = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(out.logits.reshape(-1, V), target.reshape(-1))
shifted = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(out.logits[..., :-1, :].reshape(-1, V), target[..., 1:].reshape(-1))

print("model loss      :", out.loss.item())   # 4.612360
print("CE vs labels    :", aligned.item())    # 4.542673  (correct)
print("CE vs labels[1:] :", shifted.item())   # 4.612360  (what the model actually computes)
```

The model loss matches the double-shifted CE, not the aligned CE.

### Expected behavior

Loss should be computed directly against `labels` with a plain `CrossEntropyLoss` (matching `WhisperForConditionalGeneration`, `BartForConditionalGeneration`, and the fixed Moonshine), with no second shift. Logits and `generate()` are unchanged, and `-100` stays ignored.

title: [Gemma4] Fix dtype casting for quantized vision/audio embedders (same as #46904)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 4.52.0.dev0 (main branch)
- - Platform: Linux
- - - Python version: 3.10
- - - - PyTorch version: 2.x with bitsandbytes

### Who can help?

@zucchini-nlp @SunMarc

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

aPR #46904 fixed the unsafe `tensor.to(weight.dtype)` pattern in `gemma4_unified` but the same bug exists in `gemma4` (non-unified).

**Buggy code in `src/transformers/models/gemma4/modular_gemma4.py`:**

### 1. `Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder.forward()` (line 587)
```python
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values.to(self.input_proj.weight.dtype))
```

### 2. `Gemma4AudioSubSampleConvProjectionLayer.forward()` (line 346)
```python
hidden_states = self.conv(hidden_states.to(self.conv.weight.dtype))
```

When loaded with quantization (e.g. `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True)`), `self.input_proj.weight.dtype` returns `torch.uint8`/`torch.int8` instead of a float type. Casting `pixel_values` (float) to int silently destroys the image/audio data — values like `0.73` become `0`.

The model then produces garbage outputs with no error or warning.

**Reproduction:**
```python
from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor, BitsAndBytesConfig
import torch

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained("google/gemma-4-12b-it", quantization_config=bnb_config)
# Vision/audio inputs will be silently cast to int, producing wrong outputs
```

**Fix (same pattern as #46904):**```pythonif (target_dtype := self.input_proj.weight.dtype).is_floating_point:
    pixel_values = pixel_values.to(target_dtype)
hidden_states = self.input_proj(pixel_values)
```

### Expected behavior

The model should only cast inputs to the weight dtype when the weight dtype is a floating-point type. When quantized (int8/int4), the dtype cast should be skipped, preserving the original float values. This is the behavior already implemented in `gemma4_unified` via PR #46904.

### Tasks

### Reproduction

PR #41251 introduced early returns in `create_masks_for_generate` that change the return type from dict to a bare value when `effective_config.layer_types` has a single pattern or contains unknown types. This silently breaks model forward methods that rely on `isinstance(attention_mask, dict)` to detect whether the mask was already prepared by generate().

Before #41251

When effective_config.layer_types was present, create_masks_for_generate always returned a dict mapping layer type names to masks:

```python
# Line ~1530 before PR#41251
if hasattr(effective_config, "layer_types"):
    causal_masks = {}
    for layer_pattern in set(effective_config.layer_types):
        causal_masks[layer_pattern] = LAYER_PATTERN_TO_MASK_FUNCTION_MAPPING[layer_pattern](**mask_kwargs)
    return causal_masks  # Always a dict
```

After #41251

The PR added two early-return paths that skip the dict wrapper:

```python
if any(layer_type not in LAYER_PATTERN_TO_MASK_FUNCTION_MAPPING for layer_type in layer_patterns):
    return attention_mask  # Bare value — could be None, 2D tensor, etc.

if len(layer_patterns) == 1:
    return LAYER_PATTERN_TO_MASK_FUNCTION_MAPPING[next(iter(layer_patterns))](**mask_kwargs)  # Bare value
```

Concrete impact: Qwen3

`Qwen3Model.forward` checks whether the mask was already prepared using isinstance:

```python
# src/transformers/models/qwen3/modeling_qwen3.py line ~404
if not isinstance(causal_mask_mapping := attention_mask, dict):
    # Mask not yet prepared — call create_causal_mask again
    causal_mask_mapping = {"full_attention": create_causal_mask(**mask_kwargs)}
```

Before PR#41251, `create_masks_for_generate` returned a dict like `{"full_attention": None}`. Qwen3Model.forward's isinstance(attention_mask, dict) check passed, and the model used the pre-computed mask (None) directly with is_causal=True.

After PR#41251, with the early return `if len(layer_patterns) == 1: return ...`, the function returns bare None instead of a dict. Qwen3Model.forward enters the non-dict branch, and calls `create_causal_mask(attention_mask=None)` a second time. In this second call, `attention_mask=None produces padding_mask=None`, which causes `_can_skip_causal_mask_xpu` to fall back to a conservative path that cannot determine the mask is purely causal, so it falls through to building a full 4D mask with `is_causal=False`. It cause a significant performance regression.


Script: 
[repro_contract.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29470254/repro_contract.py)


### Expected behavior

Revert early return path or fix Qwen mask script.

title: Add AstroCLIP model support
body:
### Feature request

I'd like to add AstroCLIP to Transformers.

AstroCLIP is a CLIP-style dual encoder for astronomy data. It aligns galaxy image
cutouts with galaxy spectra using a DINOv2 image encoder, a SpecFormer spectrum
encoder, cross-attention pooling heads and a symmetric contrastive loss.

Paper: https://huggingface.co/papers/2310.03024

The implementation I am preparing includes:

- `AstroClipConfig` and `AstroClipSpectrumConfig`
- `AstroClipModel` and `SpecFormerModel`
- image and spectrum preprocessing classes
- `AstroClipProcessor`
- Auto class registration
- docs and model tests
- a checkpoint conversion script for the upstream Lightning checkpoints

Validation against the upstream checkpoints:

- SpecFormer: 79 mapped keys, 0 skipped, strict load passes.
- AstroCLIP: 446 mapped source keys, 542 target tensors, 0 skipped, strict load
  passes (542/542 model keys).
- The converted model reloads via `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and
  `AutoModel.from_pretrained`.
- Fixed-input parity against the upstream implementation passes at `rtol=1e-4`,
  `atol=1e-5` for image embeddings, spectrum embeddings, logits and contrastive
  loss.

Before opening a PR: does AstroCLIP fit the current model scope and would you
prefer the work split (e.g. model implementation first, checkpoint/model-card
publication separately)?

title: AutoProcessor.from_pretrained retries HTTP 429 responses multiple times for every config file when using HF_ENDPOINT
body:
### System Info

(uv run transformers env fails with name « CompletionCreateParamsStreaming » is not defined, but this is a separate issue) 

- transformers 5.12.1
- windows 11 

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez 

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [x] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [ ] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

When `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained()` is used with a proxy configured through the `HF_ENDPOINT` environment variable, the method retries every request that receives an HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) response several times before moving on.

For example, it attempts up to 5 GET requests for each of the following files:
- processor_config.json
- tokenizer_config.json
- tokenizer.json
and several other optional configuration files

Eventually, from_pretrained() returns but the repeated retries significantly increase the loading time and flood the logs with 429 errors.

I'm not sure whether this is intended behavior, but retrying multiple times on every 429 for optional files seems excessive. It makes me wonder whether the retry logic is being applied correctly / too broadly.

```py
import os

os.environ["HF_ENDPOINT"] = "https://<your-proxy>"

from transformers import AutoProcessor

AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(
    "facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m"
)
```

### Expected behavior

Either avoid retrying optional files after repeated 429 responses, or
Retry more selectively, so that model loading does not incur dozens of failed requests before returning.

title: Add RWKV7 model support
body:
### Feature request

### Model description

I would like to propose adding RWKV7 support to Transformers.

RWKV7 is the latest generation of the RWKV recurrent language model family. It is a causal language model with recurrent state updates, but it is not compatible with the existing `rwkv` implementation in Transformers, which targets earlier RWKV variants. RWKV7 has different token-mixing/state-update formulas, different checkpoint structure, and different configuration conventions, so I think it should be added as a separate model family under `src/transformers/models/rwkv7` rather than extending the existing `rwkv` model with another version flag.

The proposed Transformers integration would include:

- `Rwkv7Config`
- `Rwkv7Model`
- `Rwkv7ForCausalLM`
- `Rwkv7Tokenizer`
- Auto class registration
- checkpoint conversion from upstream RWKV-LM `.pth` checkpoints to Transformers `safetensors`
- tokenizer conversion to standard Transformers assets, including `vocab.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `merges.txt`, and `chat_template.jinja`
- tests for model loading, tokenizer round-trip, generation, and numerical parity against the upstream RWKV-LM implementation

I found the open RWKV6 PR https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/34918 while checking for overlapping work. This RWKV7 proposal is not meant to duplicate that PR: RWKV7 uses a different architecture/checkpoint format from the currently supported RWKV implementation and from the RWKV6 work. I am opening this issue first to coordinate before submitting a PR.

Local validation has been performed against the upstream RWKV-LM implementation:

- converted RWKV7 checkpoints can be loaded through the Transformers `AutoModelForCausalLM` path
- greedy generation was compared against RWKV-LM
- logits and top-k token ordering were compared against RWKV-LM
- tokenizer encode/decode behavior was checked after converting the upstream vocabulary to Transformers tokenizer files
- the initial implementation prioritizes a plain PyTorch path for numerical correctness; optimized kernels can be discussed separately if maintainers prefer

### Open source status

- [x] The model implementation is available
- [x] The model weights are available

### Provide useful links for the implementation

Reference implementation:

https://github.com/BlinkDL/RWKV-LM

Official RWKV7 model repository:

https://huggingface.co/BlinkDL/rwkv7-g1

Example upstream checkpoints:

- https://huggingface.co/BlinkDL/rwkv7-g1/resolve/main/rwkv7-g1d-0.1b-20260129-ctx8192.pth
- https://huggingface.co/BlinkDL/rwkv7-g1/resolve/main/rwkv7-g1g-1.5b-20260526-ctx8192.pth

Example converted Transformers-format checkpoint:

https://huggingface.co/chinoll/rwkv7-g1d-0.1b

Related existing Transformers RWKV work:

- Existing RWKV implementation: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/src/transformers/models/rwkv
- Open RWKV6 PR: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/34918

### Motivation

RWKV7 checkpoints are already available on the Hugging Face Hub, but they currently require custom code to load and run. Native Transformers support would make these models easier to use with the standard `AutoModelForCausalLM`, tokenizer, generation, conversion, and downstream fine-tuning workflows.

### Your contribution

I can contribute the initial PyTorch implementation, tokenizer support, checkpoint conversion script, converted test checkpoint, documentation, and tests. I have also run local checks against the upstream RWKV-LM implementation and can include those results in the PR.
